texts:
Welcome to our two accountants, who only have missionary-position sex, and which happens only between the hours of 9pm and 11pm every Friday night after both parties are tipsy enough for someone to make the first move. At least they turn the light on now.
Make no mistake, they’re happy, but one wonders how much ball-breaking fun is had here. Then again, perhaps that’s none of our business? In which case ignore what anyone says about you both, which is what we should all be doing anyway.

Come 2070, there is a fair amount of evidence to suggest artificial intelligence will not only match that of humans, but that there might even be robots having relationships with us. And if they can do that with humans, and let’s face it, not all humans are the brightest sparks, then it’s not too fanciful to imagine one robot might be able to fall in love with another robot. Then what? We don’t know, but this pair might be a nice example of such a relationship. At the very least, you’d be surprised if they ever fought wouldn’t you? And if they did, the whole thing would only last a micro-second or so. So, while something might be lacking, you can’t suggest they don’t have the potential to get on well.

With so much organisation in the building, where is the space for sporadic, spontaneous silliness? Then again, maybe these two deplore chaos so much that they’d be very happy existing inside a very systematic way of life. Have either of you seen the movie Tron? Anyway, we have no idea if they ever feel the need for holidays. They might make a tremendous pair of lawyers, actually, because we can easily picture them in bed in a heated moment, not screaming out each other’s name, but joyously yelling out the case number of some pivotal court ruling that they both appreciated greatly, and which influenced their respective career choices. What ever blows your hair back, kids.

On a good day these two are theoretically terrific, albeit lacking a bit of zaniness. Metaphorically, these two are like a couple of old sea captains who have spent so long staring at marine charts and weather maps that they know no other way of communicating. Sure, we’re exaggerating just a little here, but then again, we all know how much a diligent and conscientious captain loves being told what is wrong with his ship and how to manage his vessel better than he or she is - NOT. Either way it makes for an interesting passage for all those on board, and they should take a life jacket just in case.

Remember the last time one of them stood up in a public place and declared their undying love for the other via a poem? Oh yeah, that never happened did it because they were too busy in the cellar scribbling down their inventory of wines, making sure it was up to date and turning those that were due. Thaaat’s right….we remember now: the thought of a romantic poem flashed passed the mind of one them later, after a few glasses of that famed Western Australian cab sav they tried, but it was quickly dismissed as being a little childish. Oh well. Maybe next year.

And here we are confronted with a police officer, (1), who works tirelessly for the Domestic Violence unit, and the social worker, (2), who is so compassionate that they give out their private home phone number to anyone who they consider might need it. Sometimes even as they do something as banal as walking down the street.
There is no question that they’re on the same mission, these two, but do they spend enough time looking after themselves? It’s a good question. They’re almost like those car mechanics who are famous for doing a good job at a very reasonable rate, but drive around in a rusted, beat-up shit box. 
In romance, these two have it theoretically made, but if they don’t take the time for self-maintenance then they might struggle.

There are probably many schools in which the principal, (1), has a fantastic, loving relationship with one of his or her teachers, (2). The shared desire to help the kids is beneficial for the whole place. Yes, (1) is better at dealing with the big picture as a manager and they are complimented very well by (2), who is much better down at the coal face, in light of their warm and more amiable approach to people and students alike. Indeed, sometimes (2) carries the woes of some of her students around with them such that they might forget their own worries. Ditto, they might even see (1) as being a little callous for not feeling the same way, where as (1) might feel like (2) cares more about the students than them. But, they seem to come around in the end because the school’s best students always do very well and no one is talking of quitting just yet.

If you imagine (1) as the skilled surgeon then (2) is their attentive and industrious head nurse, and these two form a powerful team. (For those of you from a slightly older generation, think Hawkeye and Margaret from M.A.S.H, although you might need to swap the genders.) Anyway, these two are on the same team and have the same goals in mind. There might be the odd temper tantrum from (1) who doesn’t understand the real post-op needs of patients like (2) does, when all they want to do is drag (2) to the Officer’s Mess for a drink, and likewise (2) might be occasionally disappointed that (1) has switched off now they’ve taken their scrubs off. Nothing is perfect and neither are these two, but they provide benefits to more than just each other and in this case the sum of the parts is definitely greater than the whole.

(1), the head architect and (2), the chief engineer, seem to miraculously get the tower block built on time and under budget every time. Shared values: that’s what makes these two tick. The only downside is that they sometimes get so caught up in either union disputes or arguments with materials suppliers that they occasionally forget that they are sharing a loving, personal relationship with each other. They usually come around in the end, and testament to this is the fact that most of the buildings they produce win some kind of award. And the joy they both receive at the finish, seeing happy people walking in and out the front doors of their ‘baby’, provides an immense amount of shared pride. Not bad. Not bad at all.

These two should run a yoga/mediation retreat. (1) is organised and has grand ideals of running a smooth, positive organisation like this, and let’s face it, there needs to be some organisation, and (2), as a reasonably well known local yoga instructor and part-time intuit, was born to help people get in touch with themselves and to help facilitate any healing which some visitors might need. It’s a nice combination. Both enjoy doing genuine good in the world, although (1) doesn’t go in for the mediation that (2) swears by, and who repeatedly encourages (1) to try it out again. Does this grate a little? Sometimes, yes. On the flip-side, (2) often spends so long discussing the particulars of some visitors’ woes that (1) feels like they are being forgotten about. This is just how it is sometimes. They’ll be okay. Namaskar.

These two are wonderful. They wake up every morning, pull out the day’s agenda (which was decided at least 24hours beforehand) and off they go, diligently ticking off every task with a big grin of satisfaction. And it’s not all just about (1) and (3) either. They want to do good in the world, and this is how they aim to achieve excellence: have a plan directed at their (mutual) goals and bloody well take action to achieve them. 
Too right. 
In fact, is there a more dynamic, target-oriented couple? We’re not sure. 
They talk, they share their problems and behind closed doors they probably have orgasm competitions, at least, we hope this is a distinct possibility.

Watching these two walk out of the building is like watching a successful Prime Minister, (3), stride to the microphone next to a visiting despotic President, (1), whom they happen to be hosting. The speeches are tremendous, broadcast live across the world, and you would never pick that (3) is slightly humoured by the over zealous (1), who, let’s face it, isn’t quite as laid back. Nice to know, however, that it isn’t all about the limelight for these two. Yes, they love the cameras and the barrage of questions fired at them from the press gallery afterwards, but they both really do aim to make their respective countries better places to live in, and they know that they can help each other tremendously. It’s actually just fun to be in the same space as the two of them, and we’re pretty sure prosperity and lower taxes are what’s in store for all of us. “Three cheers for (1) and (3)! Hoorah!”

These two would make wonderful leaders of a cub scout or a girl guide pack, on the proviso that the local newspapers come out and do an article about them. Why? Because each of them seeks to help out and generally do some good, and what better way to be seen to be legendary by society than by helping the youth of the nation! (1) is better at the hands-on details of dealing with kids in canoes, as well as subtly providing general moral guidance, while (3) is far more adept at handling, meeting and greeting visiting photographers, as well as placating worried parents who may have heard a rumour that the lake they are camping at contains crocodiles. Sure, attending large groups of kids requires a lot of energy and at night there is barely any left for these two to be able to share some special intimate time together, but they don’t mind. Most of the kids are happy and, tomorrow, the group photo with these two at the front is going to be on the front page of the paper. Glory!

Is that trumpets we hear in the back ground? By god it is, and here comes Cleopatra, (3), exultant Egyptian leader and goddess, her throne hoisted on the shoulders of mute slaves! What a sight! Oh hang on, and here comes Marc Antony, (1), hoisted in a similar fashion, except he has an entire garrison of the Roman army behind him. What a magnificent sight! 
“Oh, what’s that you say? I can’t hear you for the trumpets…” 
“I said, did you know they’re a couple?”
“Really? Well there you go. They’ll do us proud, won’t they?”
“Yep. He suggested building an aqueduct between Carthage and Alexandria for her, and she agreed to it straight away.”
“Great, but hang on, how do you know that?’
“Cos I’m going to help build it. They’ll even feed us.”
“Ahhh, life is good then.” 
Amen.

These two are good. Think Dave Stewart and Annie Lennox (Eurythmics), think James Watson and Francis Crick (discovered DNA), think Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire (they danced a bit). Do you get the picture? We don’t feel like comparing apples with these two, there’s no real need, suffice to say (1) and (3) are a rather stunning team and they have our congratulations. They’re driven, organised, share a similar goal and in a perfect world they back each other up, being fully aware of the foibles of the other. So, maybe just grab yourself a comfy seat, sit back and watch them do their thing. Too right.

Like an open-minded Nazi, (1), who has fallen in love with a psychic and practicing Buddhist, (4), these two might be a tremendous pairing purely because of the differences of philosophy they each bring, but it will take a lot of work to get the relationship functioning smoothly. (4) is into navel gazing and intimacy-craving, whereas (1) is into getting themselves organised and working hard. Can it work? Well, of course, but we’re climbing a mountain here kiddies and you’ll need to be prepared for the inevitable run of bad weather. We suggest you don’t give up until someone suddenly isn’t there any more. In fact, you know what.....aah, actually, don't worry about it.

We know that any combination of two people has the capacity to work, but this one really is more problematic than most. Why? Because getting anything done here is like observing a financial manager, (1), home from a busy day at the office, attempt and locate and book a table at an appropriate restaurant for (4), who is adamant that the feng shui be just right, and not just any restaurant will do. And it seems most scenarios in their lives butt up against this disparity of life-approaches. (4) will get frustrated that (1) doesn’t understand their point of view and (1) will be saddened that they two of them can never seem to do anything smoothly. Our advice? Just don’t!

Cats: they’re a fascinating creature, but have you ever tried to shoo a group of them over to one part of the room, or perhaps endeavoured to heard them towards a doorway? That’s right, its bloody impossible, and this is the dilemma faced by these two. As a staunchly independent and free-thinking soul, and as brilliant as they occasionally are, (4) has a hard time not doing what they please and certainly expressing how they feel, whenever they want, and they definitely resent being badgered into anything. (1) on the other hand has morals and self-discipline, and doesn’t mind adhering to a plan if that is what was agreed upon earlier. So, how to solve this little conundrum?

Day one of the ski trip - (4)’s idea - and (1) is ready early: goggles and helmet on, appropriate jacket, trousers and gloves on, lifts passes in pocket, skis at the ready, bottle of water and sandwich tucked away. 
“Okay, let’s go,” (1) says, about to blast out the door.
“Just a minute,” (4) replies. “I’m nearly ready, but can we go to the run at the other side of the mountain?”
“What are you talking about?” asks (1). “Isn’t this where you wanted to start?”
“I know,” says (4), “but I think we might better off on the other side.
“Why do you say that? You were here last year! This is why we came here? And you’re a better skier than me!”

Indeed, this kind of thing seems to happen whenever they do anything together.

Yes, there is a touch of oil and water about these two. (4) is like a wild horse who likes to run with the breeze through their mane, galloping over mountain and through rivers with gay abandon, and going where the winds and the seasons direct them, bounded by nothing. (1) on the other hand may very well have a touch of OCD about them, in that they strive for perfection, abhor chaos and the unknown, and find a great deal of pleasure in walking back in the front door to discover the house in perfect order. So, you tell us, how do you think they’ll go when aiming at any kind of relationship? Our advice? If you’re matched sexually, knock yourselves out and have a fab time, but go your separate ways after breakfast.

Like two highly intelligent and inquisitive creatures hailing from different planets altogether, their respective aims and desires are ostensibly the same, it’s just that the nuances of language, and therefore perceived intent, take a long time to coincide. Both are highly curious and analysing their environment is something they appear to be well-developed for. And they have a sense of humour, though (5) is far more adept at dealing with the unknown than (1). 
And, to be honest, (5) occasionally deliberately provides a little chaos, just to see what will happen. It’s a good way to test a hypothesis, though this often angers (1), and this is but one of many mis-communications.

These two are like the sorcerer and the apprentice. Yes, magic looks like a lot of mystical wonderment, but in actual fact it’s all just physics and momentum undertaken with deftness, nonchalance and speed. Our sorcerer, (5), whose face one rarely sees, knows all the tricks, is ruffled by very little, be it a poor audience reaction or a slightly slashed belly, and is constantly on the look out for new and high quality acts which they can use as part of his or her show. (1) on the other hand is doing very well to keep up, and they have a few tricks of their own, although their capacity to absorb the unexpected into their routine might require some attention, and we’re not sure if this is something that can be taught or not. Maybe the same stage isn’t something these two should be considering? But, they definitely put on a good show, at least for a short while.

(5) is like the unseen union mastermind who doesn’t mind receiving the odd bribe, if only for the fact that the entire system is corrupt and true altruism, they know, will only bring dissatisfaction, and a failure to achieve anything meaningful. (1) on the other hand has just left university and regularly marches in protest - workers’ rights, land rights, the environment, etc etc - and they were delighted to join the union with the hope of making a real difference to the poor and downtrodden of the world. What is (5) to do? They know the truth of the system will kill (1), but not to tell them will only destroy them in the long run, which is probably worse. So they have no choice. Hence, in terms of a relationship, is disappointment inevitable? If (1) is strong, smart and flexible enough, not necessarily.

If you imagine (1) as the young race car driver who is newly arrived into the team, and who carries a reputation, then (5) is the head mechanic who knows the ins and outs of this car better than anyone. Sure, (1) is the soul who sits behind the wheel and risks life and limb to race the thing, but (5) can tell exactly how it’s being driven and knows precisely how it can be driven better. This is cutting edge technology we’re talking about and the computers don’t lie, neither does the amount of wear on the cylinders and the tyres, and while (5) listens intently to what (1) has to say with regards to handling and general feel - they’re not totally stupid - at the end of the day this young hoon, skilled though they are, is still extremely naive as to what this machine is capable of. So, I guess we’ll sit down and watch the race, eh? There’s bound to be a crash some time…

Ever seen the British TV show, Yes Minister? It’s old, true, but is it the funniest, most relevant political show ever made? It must be close. Anyway, if one imagines (1) as the high-minded politician who needs to be seen to be doing the right thing, and to hopefully adhere to set of morals which can be both useful and admired, then (5) is their chief advisor who knows very well the entire system is a bloody farce, and that providing a facade which appears to be intact, conscientious and transparent is vital if the government is to remain in power, and, to a lesser extent, appear to be seen to actually try and achieve something meaningful. No, (1) is not a puppet at the hands of (5) but there are certain inalienable truths which need to be told, but only at the right time, and only if required. Plausible deniability is something (1) simply doesn’t need to know about. So, marriage here?….Mmmm….not so sure.

If we imagine (1) as the decorated army lieutenant with high-minded ideals and a sense of organisation and discipline, then (6) is that soldier who, despite a fine record, was once discharged after being discovered smoking pot. Everyone was a winner probably, because no way was (6) ever going to shoot anyone, really. (They’re too humane for that kind of absurdity). 
But, out in the real world (1) appreciates (6)’s sense of humour, sometimes, as well as their sense of playfulness, so who can say how they’ll turn out? At their core they share many beliefs, it’s just the final expressions of behaviour which separates them. Perhaps all they need to do is make the decision to try? And they both joined up for a reason, yes?

Yes, we keep harping on about AI here, and where robots are heading, but if you don’t mind we’re going to use you two as another example. What do we mean? We mean that, as robots evolve they are going to arrive from the factory in stages of increasing intelligence, to the point where, maybe in 100 years or so, it might not actually be impossible to tell if someone is a robot or not. Have you seen Blade Runner and its sequel? Well, the early versions of hyper-intelligent robots will be a lot like (1): they’ll be brilliant, charming and funny, but they’ll probably be just a little too rigid in their thinking when compared to (6) - a much later version - who can toy with ideas better, adapt to change faster and be generally more sarcastic, as well as being way more likely to kill us all. Anyway, the point is, these two are very similar to one another, and us poor humans will just have to muddle along in our ignorance.

If you imagine (1) as the Park Ranger with an immaculate uniform and a penchant for keeping the rules, no matter what, then (6) is their loyal and rather more laid back colleague. On total fire band days (1) storms around the park, ensuring no rubbish is dropped on the ground and that no campfires are lit. (6), on the other hand, so long as (1) isn’t around, will happily chat with the campers and, hidden from view, toke on a quiet joint if offered but make no mistake, the welfare of the park and the campers is foremost in both their minds, and it’s a beautiful place that they both relish working in. As a team they do a wonderful job, and both compliment the other tremendously. Indeed, so long as these two are in attendance, there will be no fires, the campers will always leave happy and no rubbish will ever find its way into the local rivers. Amen.

Yep, so (1) is a stickler for protocol, they are confident and capable and generally covet an organised work station. (6) works in the same office, knows more people who work on different floors, chats to more people at the work Christmas party, and has less headaches about work after they arrive home. 
Do they both aspire to get the job done, and to do a fine job at that?
Absolutely.
Does (6) appreciate the methodology of (1) as being necessary to the group?
Yes.
Does (1) appreciate the same thing of (6)?
Yes.
Does a part of each of them respect and admire those parts in the other which are different?
Very much so. The End.

If (1) is the pilot not quite ready to skydive just yet, then (6) is the ex-pilot who gave flying away to sky dive, and who has now jumped out of planes 5,000 times. Both love being in the air, both have a very different take on how to navigate and move once they are doing their thing, and both feel just a tiny bit disappointed when their feet touch the ground. We’d imagine that, as a couple, they’ll be just fine.

Like a drug-addicted, effervescent clown, (7), having a relationship with well-paid tax attorney, (1), there is a slim chance that they might actually complement one another brilliantly, so there must be some hope, right? The fun/freedom-seeking (7) may actually encourage (1) to chill-out and take things less seriously. Likewise, (1) might aid (7) to stay focussed and to finish what they begin, but everyone doubts it, even them. Whatever happens it’ll be fun to watch and the best part is that these two will at least be well-equipped to see the humour in their own demise. Hell, it might even be the reason the universe plonked them together in the first place.

You don’t often witness a police officer falling in love with the bank robber they happened to catch, do you? Maybe that’s a good thing. Our loveable bank robber, (7), who can barely sit still for more than 10 minutes, didn’t really mind being arrested by (1). Part of them actually appreciates the work ethic and dedication (1) must have applied in order to find them in the first place. (7) simply can’t imagine being that diligent over such a long time. (1), on the other hand, might secretly wish they could go to work for one day and have the next year off, but to break the law? They’ll probably never get their head around that one. So, a fun little tryst, only, is what might be on offer here, unless (1) decides to try and help (7) break out of jail. I guess we’ll all wait for the telemovie to tell us what happened…

Seen Topgun? The original? Well, that man in the control tower who repeatedly denied Maverick permission to fly a low pass over the airfield is (1) - and don’t for a second think they don’t do a bloody fine job, without which plenty of people would die - and Maverick is (7). Anyway, that’s the short version. Are they suited romantically? ….What do YOU reckon?

And here we have (1), our King or Queen, born into the role and therefore with little thought or chance of opting out, who is obliged to maintain a certain regimented level of organisation across the realm - after all, why would a peasant farmer pay taxes to a leader who constantly cracks jokes, mucks around and seemingly has no care in the world? On the other hand, that is (7)'s job as court jester: to maintain levity and a sense of fun at all times, and to amuse and diffuse those in court who might otherwise bore us all to death. So (7) has a role to play, make no mistake, and which is usually appreciated by (1). Don’t think they don’t, it’s just that (7) is never going to be knighted, for that would mean that (1) deeply, truly and publicly adored the silly rascal. And that, ladies and gentlemen, would be what we call a scandal.

In cartoon terms, these two are like the Roadrunner and the Coyote. Do you think you can guess who is who? We’re not going to tell you, it’s so obvious. Suffice to say, being the aggressor requires planning, it requires patience and it requires intelligence, well, theoretical intelligence anyway. And what does our goofy Roadrunner have to do? Sweet bugger all. Their only aim in life is to run like the wind, smile like a bloody idiot, and frustrate those in their midst who would aim to diminish the amount of fun they are currently having. Does Coyote ever stop and admire Roadrunner’s capacity to live in this moment?….Not often. And does the Roadrunner ever take a second to appreciate the amount of preparation Coyote puts in, in order to try and catch him? …Shit no. So no, we don’t expect too much from this coupling.

Ever seen the movie 'Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'? It’s a wonderful show about a fellow who overcomes adversity to eventually save the world from tyranny, again. Well, these two are quite similar in their desires apart from one very palpable difference.
In the movie, there is one scene were Indiana Jones is forced to make a leap of faith, which will save, not only the world, sort of, but his own father’s life. If our hell-raising, truth-or-death (8) were in a similar position they would always make the jump, whereas our gutsy-but-wired-differently (1) rarely would, which (8) would take very personally.
And eventually these ACTUAL LIFE ACTION differences will spell their doom. In short, maybe these two should just keep their clothes on.

One can easily imagine (8) as a high-ranking officer in the Napoleonic wars, ardently believing in France, and being quite happy to die for his Emperor. (1) on the other hand was conscripted and while they’re all-for France doing well, and Napoleon prevailing, not to mention how much they love their uniform and the discipline the army provides, they're mostly quite happy to simply avoid being killed or injured, to not starve or freeze to death, and to eventually arrive home in one piece with a few bragging rights. That’s enough for (1), really. Yes, (1) loves the way (8) wears their heart on their sleeve, espousing death or glory, but deep down that ain’t them, and (8) would be utterly disgusted to learn that (1) doesn’t feel the same immediate passion. In short, death or miscommunication on the battlefield is highly likely.

Mmmm, might be best if these two just kiss and call it a day. (8) is like the tempestuous rock star whose dedication to the art and to the purity of what they are singing about takes precedence, and who carries a deep mistrust of anyone on the team who doesn’t have the same belief in what they’re trying to achieve together. (1), the band manager, adores the music and the general tone of what (8) sings about, but they have a different set of passions to get involved in, and the longer they can avoid an in-depth discussion as to the philosophy of the group - something (8) loves to do, and the bigger the discussion the better - the happier everyone will be. Is it inevitable that (8) will spit the dummy?…..yep.

No, (1) isn’t a coward, far from it. It’s just that the leader of the clan, (8), is, in their opinion, certifiably insane. Currently (8) is standing on a rock preaching to the whole tribe about how, tomorrow morning, when those six hundred armed U.S soldiers come galloping over that ridge, all eighty tribe members capable of fighting are going to pick up their bows and arrows and meet them head-on. While (8) rants and raves and carries on, whipping the tribe into a suicidal frenzy, (1) drops their head and whispers quietly to no one, “You’re going to get us all killed. Why don’t we just pull back into the ravine and meet up with the next tribe?” But (1) knows that uttering such a protest right now would be deemed an act of treason. So, romance? Forget it.

The head seamstress, (1), knows what they are doing and they've been at it for a long time. Their methods are faultless, their work ethic impeccable, and they always produce outstanding results for the designers who seek them out. But have they now just about had enough? Once again (8) storms into the room waving a freshly made garment in their hands, babbling on about how this design isn’t what they specified. And it’s not the first time. (1) has tried to tell (8) that what they wanted was impossible, only because the materials in use can’t be joined together in the way they wished. But it’s no use. (8) isn’t listening to reason and is starting to get hysterical, accusing (1) of incompetence and hypocrisy. Eventually, yes, (1) tells (8) that perhaps it’s time they found another designer. They’re probably right.

A nice combo’. If the two of them were charged with running the company, then (1) would do the hard-nosed negotiating while (9) would ensure the employees were looked after and that the environment wasn’t being degraded too much. (9) doesn’t handle the high-powered situations like (1) and the only issue which might arise is how each of them handle the ramifications of this deep recession we’re apparently about to walk into. Having said that, they understand each other very well, including their different roles, and one would imagine that when hardship does arrive these two will ride with the punches together, laughing as they go and reminding each other of what’s important. Best of all, after coming out the back of such trials they’d be grateful they experienced it together. Splendid.

The quintessential good cop, bad cop. Good, being (9) and bad being (1), and they do their job very well. (9) is a wonderful second in charge, if you like, who has more kudos on the street in lieu of a friendlier, more engaging nature, and (1) is better at dealing with the intricacies of a case, and plotting a method to get the bad guy or fix the problem. They solve most cases they’re involved with and the Captain, back at headquarters, feels lucky to have them on board. And so do we.

(9) and (1)’s Funeral Service. Death Might Be Wonderful, is their motto. Not only do they both believe in some kind of afterlife, but they appreciate helping out here at the finish line, and to assist families through this difficult time. True, many families are a little put off by their stance but they seem to provide real care to those remaining, and the testimonies of these people are the proof in the pudding. (1) usually deals with the organisational running of the business -  schedules, embalming rosters, hearse maintenance, etc - while (9)’s role is almost purely interpersonal. They radiate warmth and compassion even when they’re alone in the bathroom, so you can only imagine how wonderful they are at consoling grieving families. Yep, Death Might Be Wonderful is doing very well, and we expect that to continue. Bless.

Don’t you just love the corner store? And how long have (9) and (1) been running it for? Feels like forever. You can see (1) at sunrise if you’re up early enough, dragging in the newspapers and stacking up the daily milk arrivals. (9) doesn’t turn up until later, ever-ready with a smile and a bit of a yarn for whoever walks in the door. (1) deals with the books, ordering stock and all the admin, and they always keeps an eye on customers when they’re out the back, just in case (9) is too busy chatting to someone to notice one of the young kiddies stealing a chocolate bar, which happens occasionally. Little does (1) know, however, that (9) is actually very aware of everything, it’s just that they think it’s rather cute and, importantly, they believe a little theiving probably teaches kids about daring and deftness of hand. Anyway, the store is going very well and the town loves them both.

The hard-nosed reporter, (1), and the travel-weary camera person, (9), have been a great team for a while now and we don’t expect that to change. (1) always has an idea about the kind of story they want to create and (9)’s advice is vital - they’ve had far more experience on the street dealing with idiotic strangers, they're better at helping people relax, let alone setting up the best lighting. On the flipside (9) never needs to suggest anything to (1) in terms of which questions to ask because they have those specifics sussed. Better than that, (1) isn’t an arrogant twat like some reporters (9) has dealth with. They’re very happy to help setting up and, overall, they just enjoy each other's company. Actually, they’re on TV right now.

And here we are confronted with a police officer, (1), who works tirelessly for the Domestic Violence unit, and the social worker, (2), who is so compassionate that they give out their private home phone number to anyone who they consider might need it. Sometimes even as they do something as banal as walking down the street.
There is no question that they’re on the same mission, these two, but do they spend enough time looking after themselves? It’s a good question. They’re almost like those car mechanics who are famous for doing a good job at a very reasonable rate, but drive around in a rusted, beat-up shit box. 
In romance, these two have it theoretically made, but if they don’t take the time for self-maintenance then they might struggle.

There are probably many schools in which the principal, (1), has a fantastic, loving relationship with one of his or her teachers, (2). The shared desire to help the kids is beneficial for the whole place. Yes, (1) is better at dealing with the big picture as a manager and they are complimented very well by (2), who is much better down at the coal face, in light of their warm and more amiable approach to people and students alike. Indeed, sometimes (2) carries the woes of some of her students around with them such that they might forget their own worries. Ditto, they might even see (1) as being a little callous for not feeling the same way, where as (1) might feel like (2) cares more about the students than them. But, they seem to come around in the end because the school’s best students always do very well and no one is talking of quitting just yet.

If you imagine (1) as the skilled surgeon then (2) is their attentive and industrious head nurse, and these two form a powerful team. (For those of you from a slightly older generation, think Hawkeye and Margaret from M.A.S.H, although you might need to swap the genders.) Anyway, these two are on the same team and have the same goals in mind. There might be the odd temper tantrum from (1) who doesn’t understand the real post-op needs of patients like (2) does, when all they want to do is drag (2) to the Officer’s Mess for a drink, and likewise (2) might be occasionally disappointed that (1) has switched off now they’ve taken their scrubs off. Nothing is perfect and neither are these two, but they provide benefits to more than just each other and in this case the sum of the parts is definitely greater than the whole.

(1), the head architect and (2), the chief engineer, seem to miraculously get the tower block built on time and under budget every time. Shared values: that’s what makes these two tick. The only downside is that they sometimes get so caught up in either union disputes or arguments with materials suppliers that they occasionally forget that they are sharing a loving, personal relationship with each other. They usually come around in the end, and testament to this is the fact that most of the buildings they produce win some kind of award. And the joy they both receive at the finish, seeing happy people walking in and out the front doors of their ‘baby’, provides an immense amount of shared pride. Not bad. Not bad at all.

These two should run a yoga/mediation retreat. (1) is organised and has grand ideals of running a smooth, positive organisation like this, and let’s face it, there needs to be some organisation, and (2), as a reasonably well known local yoga instructor and part-time intuit, was born to help people get in touch with themselves and to help facilitate any healing which some visitors might need. It’s a nice combination. Both enjoy doing genuine good in the world, although (1) doesn’t go in for the mediation that (2) swears by, and who repeatedly encourages (1) to try it out again. Does this grate a little? Sometimes, yes. On the flip-side, (2) often spends so long discussing the particulars of some visitors’ woes that (1) feels like they are being forgotten about. This is just how it is sometimes. They’ll be okay. Namaskar.

Suddenly we’re in the cockpit in which both captain and co-pilot, of exactly equal flying time and previous qualifications, want to double check every system on the aircraft. Not only that, they want to re-check each other and they want to ensure the passengers are really, truly content with, not only their seats, but with what’s on offer on today’s menu. And if a problem arises then, glory be, will we ever get off the ground?
Back home in bed they take hours because both parties are so eager to please one another. (Rumour has it they hold foreplay-duration records in three cities, so we can only assume that someone is having some fun somewhere.) 
But seriously, someone do something, please. This is all we ask. Sure, everyone is going to be okay but will anything else actually get done? Perhaps they’re just better off being friends?

No, these two aren’t necessarily a gay couple, but if they were both men, for instance, can you imagine how long it would take them to get in the car and head out on their date? They’d each insist on holding the door open for the other, and how absurd would that look? But, you can’t deny their attentiveness. They might be better off moving to India and opening an ashram together - that might work. Maybe acquire some kids, just so some of this lavished attention can be directed elsewhere. Together these two are like a super-rich thick shake that is so sweet and viscous it’s almost impossible to get up the straw. So, good luck, but maybe you’re just too alike?

Remember that phrase, ‘too many cooks spoil the broth’? Well that phrase originated from these two. Too much of a good thing inevitably results in a bad thing, because that’s just how the universe is wired. Moderation is the key, remember. How can two people be that attentive to one another, constantly? Sure, there's a chance they’ll work, and they might have a fantastic time in bed, who knows, but in terms of a lasting relationship, they could be a bit much for each other, eventually. But good luck, all the same.

On a good day, these two are so in touch with each other that they barely even notice those around them. On a bad day, they might be just a bit too intense for one another. Is there any space allowed at all, with these two? Are negative reactions magnified out of all proportion? Do feelings of resentment linger? We don’t know and as always, potential greatness is everywhere, so don’t listen to us if don’t feel like it. For some good news, they could be amazing in bed! So that’s exciting!

We may have seen the good coop/bad routine in here somewhere before, but these two are more like the good cop/good cop couple. Have you seen them in action? They take hours to ‘interrogate’ anyone, mostly because they roll in a trolley full of biscuits, coffee and cake just to make their ‘victim’ comfortable. Half the time they end up talking about something else altogether, so much so that occasionally the person being interviewed just sits there while both of them debate and question each other. It’s bloody funny, actually. Word around the station is that one of the officers is selling tickets for those who want to come and sit behind the two-way mirror and watch the show next time it happens. Anyway, no one is perfect.

Batman and Robin, eat your heart out, because sometimes some things just work. The only caveat with this wonderful little team is that hopefully the ‘leader’, who in this case is (3), rightly acknowledges their wonderful assistant, (2). If this happens then all will be well, but honestly, they would have to be idiots to mess this relationship up. In many social settings they ooze charm, sexual satisfaction, good humour and happiness. They’re so good, in fact, that on the morning after some giant dinner party or other, while all the guests are at home and having a lazy debrief about the night that was, no one will be able to really discern the difference between either of our wonderful duo. In the memory of these people they’ll just be this delightful, stunning couple-person. Weird, eh?

Most of us are aware of how much of the land settled across the world was achieved by powerful individuals with a sense of adventure and a capacity to get the job done, and to persist in the face of adversity. And that’s great, but how often are these people - yes, we’re talking about you, (3) - propped up and assisted by those around you? We would suggest about 100% of the time, and this is the special skill of (2). But don’t worry, (3) knows this very well and both understand the roles they fulfil when it comes to both getting the sheep ready for shearing as well as looking after the mob of shearers who will attend them. Yep, they’re a fine team, these two.

If you can imagine (3) as James Bond, regardless of their sex, then we would describe (2) as Q, the wonderful, quirky and brilliant technical whizz who gives Bond all the new gadgets, which enables him to do what he does with such success. Are they a splendid team? You’re damn right they are.

This won’t take very long, because today we give you Sherlock and Holmes. That’s right, and you wouldn’t necessarily pick them in these roles, would you? We would. The dashing, charismatic (3) is ideal in their role as the brilliant and gifted sleuth, and they are ably backed up by (2), who is not only no dummy in their own right, but who takes care of important details and often lays the foundation for some wonderful discoveries. Elementary it may be for this couple, but such a pairing doesn’t arrive frequently and all we suggest is that the criminals of the world look out. Bravo!

In actuality, Superman was the foil for Lois Lane, wasn’t he? Lois had the balls and the nous, and sure, Superman had the superpowers, but it was Lois’s pure guts and initiative which drove the whole relationship, and which eventually saved the world. So there you have it. (2) is our wonderful Superman and (3) is the indomitable Lois Lane, and a wonderful duo they are. Roll the credits please.

Page one, line one: talk to each other, you two. 
Spill your guts about everything. Shine a torch into every dark cranny and spit it all out. Leave no stone unturned. Do you hear? Now read that again (2) and (4), aloud this time. In fact, keep reading it otherwise you’ll slip back into old habits and forget everything. Flush out all your insecurities and expose them to the light. Indeed, it’s probably good advice for all of us, but you two need it if you are going to survive because neediness is a useful asset for no one. 
Do that, then come back and here and we’ll have a look at you.

Here we have a social worker going out with a psychotherapist. On paper this should work, right? But perhaps the latter, (4), is just a bit too deep and intense for our more fluid and streetwise (2). Theory is important and things need to be discussed, sure, and lord knows (4)’s couch is comfortable, but at some point these theories have to move from the salon to the real world. Let us know how you get on, and remember to retain a sense of humour at all times, but being friends might be nice, eh?

Like a theoretical physicist who sets foot in a working observatory for the first time, (4) might find the reality of this remarkable piece of engineering quite daunting. The chief researcher at the facility, (2), has seen this reaction before and they are accustom to the look of fear. It’s a pretty impressive telescope, that’s for sure, and (2) is very proud of it, not to mention what it can do. But if (4) requires days of reassurance about the calculations they’ve arrived at, with regards to this star they are supposed to be studying, by the time they get to turn the telescope at the particular sun in question the whole sky would have shifted and it’ll be too late. So, what to do? We don’t know. Maybe go back and re-calibrate for twelve years into the future.

Once again we have an issue on the work site. Our resident environmentalist and bird-lover, (4), is standing in front of a large tree which, (2), head of town planning, needs to cut down. They don’t want to cut it down, really, and all they’re trying to do is stop the local cyclists from being killed by a falling limb, which is inevitable because the tree is now truly old, and the council can’t afford to be sued. So, (2) has no choice but to listen to (4), who sensitivity on this issue knows no bounds, but what can they do? Yes, they’ve tried explaining about saving cyclists’ lives and all (4) does is start ranting about how there are too many people on the planet. And round and round we go. Is anyone else sick of this argument?

And here we have the renowned, reclusive artist, (4), humorous on the surface and definitely talented, chatting to the owner of the local art gallery, (2), who loves showcasing as many local artists as they can. Obviously, (2) is way more social than (4), and they’re very aware that catering to the various needs of some artists is an exercise in diplomacy, almost, no matter how much they love their work. And it seems this is what might be developing here. (4) is quirky and brilliant, no question, but (2) is in a bind  because while they don’t have the resources to demarcate an entire section of the gallery to (4)’s work, they desperately want it hanging in the gallery. How do they solve this issue? Anyone?

What have we got here? A quick-run thing or a crack at long-term love and greatness? If it’s the former we’ve no suggestions - you’ll work out the opposing mysteries one way or the other soon enough - but if it’s the latter then you both need to get out your geological survey equipment. You’ll need your night goggles, make sure your first aid kit is up to date and get your hands on a good solid machete. No, not to attack the other with, more to slash your way through what each of you will consider to be a rather dense, alien and challenging jungle. You, (2), are sensitive and caring and warm while you, (5), are the lone, dedicated seeker for the sake of the journey. “What is real?” is a question (5) asks all the time. You ready for that (2)? But, you never know till you give it a go. You’re almost two different species, so good luck.

We don’t mean to get morbid, but how often during WW II would have some Nazi ordered a peace-loving German soldier to shoot the hapless Jewish person standing in front of them, when the soldier in question has not only never hated any Jewish people at all, but is/has fallen in love with one of them? Honestly, what is it with human beings? Anyway, in some twisted way, could we imagine (5) as the dispassionate, single-minded Nazi, and the hapless soldier, who either has to do their job or be shot themselves, as (2)? Yes, we could. So, yes, good luck with this little romance!

The regulations stipulate that only so many people can stay over night in the homeless shelter due to the possible fire hazard, yet how does the person on reception, (2), knock back a young mum and her child when it’s cold outside? And of course, this has to occur right when the government inspector, (5), is making a routine visit. Both are only trying to do their job, and (5) would love more than anything to see this young family get a place tonight, but how would everyone feel if the nightmare happened due to overcrowding, and a fire did actually start? How can (5) possibly explain the potential horror of that outcome to these people? And you can’t argue with the maths. So what happens?….(2) is crying that they can’t say yes, the young mum is crying because she and her daughter have no where to stay, and (5) is even holding back the tears. Some problems are just too hard to deal with, eh?

(5) and (2) hop in the car and prepare to drive around the corner to visit a friend, and they’re only driving because it’s raining. (2) is behind the wheel because (5) has had a couple of wines, even though they’re only travelling 300 metres. (5) does their seat belt up and (2) doesn’t bother. 
“Are you going to do your seat belt up?” (5) asks.
“Nup, we’re just going around the corner.”
“Do you know that most car accidents happen close to home?”
“Nope.”
“Well they do, so do your seat belt up.”
“But I don’t feel like it. We’re not going far.”
And there ensues a mighty argument, which is only compounded by the weather. 
The End.

And once again we are cast into the future where, (5), the lovely and venerable house robot is trying to comfort it’s owner, (2), who has just broken up with their human partner and is sitting in the kitchen, sobbing. 
“What’s wrong, master?” (5) asks.
“Oh it’s nothing. I have a broken heart, that’s all.”
“Oh my god!” yells (5), who closes their eyes for one second before opening them again. “Don’t worry, I’ve just put a call out to an ambulance. Arrival time, seven minutes and forty seconds.”
“What? No, no, cancel that immediately! I’m not going to die, I just have a broken heart.”
“But master,” (5) says, concerned, “What do you mean?”

And there ensues a long, convoluted discussion, which is never going to have a satisfactory resolution.

These two would do well as a couple of Mormans because their devotion to duty and to one another is commendable. Solid commitment: this is what will work for these two. Pant-dropping, quick-sex-behind-the-barn isn’t really part of the equation here. Is that sad? Well, who can say. (6) will get occasionally pissed off with themselves and the world, and during these times (2) just needs to chill and not chase after them too much when (6) craves a little space. The thing is, is dependability the only criteria that’s important to each of you? If that’s the case then go get married, immediately, but there’s more excitement and magic in life to be had.

When they’re good, these two are great. So long as (6) has a little self-confidence and doesn’t over-think things, then (2) can be a wonderful, encouraging foil. But if (2) is the manager of the chemist and their chief pharmacist, (6), is in a sketchy mood, then (2) will feel like they have to manage not only the complaining customers, whose ailments seem to cover the whole spectrum of human woe, but both the shop and the dispensary and who has time for that? Mutual respect is important in life for all of us, but it’s definitely important here. Lose that and these two are screwed.

Were these two every incredibly turned on by one another, or, as we suspect may have been the case, was it a situation of gradual admiration and familiarity growing to a point where they seemingly had no choice but to take it to the next level? And there’s nothing wrong with that, is there?…

Maybe you believe in reincarnation and maybe you don’t, we’re not even sure we do, but for the sake of an example, let’s take (6) and (2). So, let’s presume, perhaps stupidly, that reincarnation exists, then one may not be totally incorrect by suggesting that (2) has been around a few more times than (6). Now, this is no criticism of (6), not by a long shot, it’s just that (2) is better at observing the bigger picture and (6) has a greater tendency to shut down if a situation isn’t to their liking. No, it not like this all the time, and they both have aspirations for a contented and loving home and family life, so, as ever, potential greatness is always just around the corner, but (2) is better at looking out, rather than looking in. Does that make sense?

Does (6) ever display the propensity for loving a bit of self-induced melodrama? And does (2) ever tire of this kind of self-absorption? The answer to both questions is a yes, but the variations on a theme take up way more space than we have room for here today. When (6) is good, they’re great, and when they’re down in the dumps they’re useless because they need constant attention and reinforcement. Fortunately (2) is good at this, and loves helping out, especially those they care about, but not if it carries on for too long. Does that sound familiar? No? Good, then I pronounce you husband and wife, or husband and husband, or wife and wife. Congratulations!

(2) is the kind of romantic who insists albatrosses mate for life, while (7) knows that, deep down, albatrosses, male and female, are wonderful tarts and occasionally excellent actors, and these disparate opinions sum these two up. (7)’s joie de vivre is adored by (2), who find them terribly exciting. Likewise (7) loves how (2) can calm them down and keep their eyes pointed at the job at hand, but often the greater level of intimacy required by (2) is too constrictive for our bouncing (7). Having said that, they generate an incredible amount of warmth for those around them and perhaps this is their gift for the world? Maybe they should consider opening an orphanage somewhere?

Yep, these two can be fantastic together. True, (7) is hardly ever home because there always seems to be some function which needs either attending or organising, and when they are home (2) is often on the phone to a friend in crisis - and lord knows (2) is a wonderful, caring shoulder to cry on - but they manage to find a way. And when they are home together and (2) isn’t on the phone, so long as they are attentive to each other then there is no reason why these two won’t go a long way. Amen.

This couple is often the life of the party. (7) does the entertaining, whether they mean to or not, and invariably (2) winds up helping at least one person who has a problem that they need to get off their chest, which they enjoy. Usually, (2) is very aware that (7) needs their space and likewise, (7) knows that (2) needs more intimacy that they are probably accustom to providing, but the generous nature of both of them somehow manages to figure out a solution which makes everyone happy most of the time. And that’s the secret for all us, right?

The only date on the calendar that presents a problem for these two is that of their wedding anniversary. Why? Because (7) barely remembers it, in lieu of the fact they don’t seem to remember much about anything, and (2) will always have a deeper need for their love and affection to be actively recognised. Question is, is this something that will strike a unrecoverable wedge between them? The answer, we think, is a resounding no, but it’s probably a salient little lesson for (7). Just remember (7), yes, you ‘re the centre of the show, but deep down you know this is a selfish load of shit, don’t you? Anyway, you two will be alright. And (2), our advice, if it really bothers you, just get (7) hammered one night and lead them to a tattoo parlour so they can get the date tattooed on their arm, or something.

And here we find our charismatic and skilled coffee maker, (7), in a fine mood. The coffee is coming out of the machine nicely, the milk is frothing easily, but not too much, and as ever, the patrons are regularly complimenting them on their fine brews. But why hasn’t the boss, (2), mentioned anything about how good their coffee is yet? (7) is beginning to worry. (2) on the other hand is in charge of this town's busiest cafe, and they have more than one task to attend to at any given time. Sure, their morning coffee was lovely, but with all they have to do, how or even should (7) constantly need to be told how wonderful they are? They’ll figure it out, we imagine, but mostly, and like the patrons sitting around looking smug and content, we just enjoy the energy these two bring to the establishment. And we’ll be back tomorrow watch them do it all again.

These two are reasonably well-suited. (2) acts as a calming soul and the source of sound advice for the leader of the pack, (8), who in turn receives doting rock-star adulation as they crash their way through life. And this leads us to a thought: Perhaps, metaphorically, there is a chance (2) eventually feels like they are living with the belligerent and uncaring town drunk. (2) is sensitive, while, comparatively, (8) is anything but, unless you’re talking to (8). We suppose if (2) was a just a little more thick-skinned and (8) just a few notches of volume quieter, and no doubt these specimens exist in the wild, then they’d be a perfect, synchronous match. Alas, this might be hard work but both of them are used to dealing with obstacles. 
(Pssst, quick little secret: these two actually need an obstacle, so they’re better suited than they think they are, just don’t tell them that.)

So, there’s an old Chinese farmer and one day his only horse, a stallion, busts out of its enclosure and escapes. The locals hear the news and they all say to him, “Gee, that’s bad.”
“Yeah, maybe,” the old farmer says.
Next day, the stallion comes back and brings with it five wild horses. The locals hear the news and they all say to him, “Gee, you must be thrilled. You’re so lucky!”
“Yeah, maybe,” the old farmer says. 
Next day, the farmer’s son, while trying to break-in one of the new horses, falls off and breaks his leg. The locals come around and all say, “Gee, that’s bad. Who will help you in the fields now? That’s so unlucky.”
“Yeah, maybe,” the old farmer says.
Next day, the army recruiting officer comes to his house hoping to conscript his son, but leaves when he sees the cast on his leg. The locals here the news and tell the old farmer, “Gee, you must glad. You’re so lucky.”
“Yeah, maybe.” Etc, etc, etc.
Yes, it's an old story, but welcome to the non-stop roller coaster that is (8) and (2). They’ll work it out one way or another.

Many philosophers will tell you that life is one long continuous sine wave. There are ups and there are downs, and you can be certain that if life is good right now, at some point not too far away it probably won’t be, and so it goes around again. We imagine that this is what things might be like for (8) and (2) here. Disregarding their sexual compatibility, they are quite similar - passionate, sensitive and proactive - and so they have a lot in common, such that if they are in concert with each other then anything is possible. (2) is far more compassionate to the needs of others, however, and while this probably doesn’t matter for most of the time, the occasionally selfish ideals of (8) frustrate and disappoint (2) greatly. It’s as if (8) is a race horse wearing blinkers living in their own reality. Usually, with time and discussion, things are recoverable, and we wonder if it’s this too-and fro-ing actually bonds them? Although it's probably more important to (8) than to (2). We just don’t know.

If (8) is the President and ego maniac, then (2) is the speech writer who made them famous. Would (8) ever realise and acknowledge this? Maybe, but probably not. We do know that (2) is just about sick of being embarrassed by their leader, that’s for sure. After all, (2) has their own life to live, and they might be a little tired of having their lives defined by what (8) is doing. Amen.

If you imagine (8) as Rocky Balboa then (2) is their devoted and loving little trainer. If you spoke to each of them privately, they would tell you that they put up with a hell of a lot of whinging and complaining from the other person, which we suggest you all ignore. Question is, is this a fair and reasonable relationship for either of them? Well, (8) is certainly going nowhere without the attention and adulation they receive from (2) and, likewise, (2) was born to help others be better and to encourage others to greatness. So, together, will they win the heavy weight championship of the world? They’re certainly a pretty good team and it looks like we’ll all find out: Madison Square Garden, this Friday night. Be there or be square…

Perhaps (2) and (9) were siblings, or mother and daughter or something, in a past life? It’s like a yogi master going out with a Zen Buddhist. With so much warmth, generosity and consideration in the room it’s difficult to imagine either of them raising their voice over anything. “Are they telepathic?” is a question many friends ask of them. These same friends also presume they either sleep or meditate a lot because of how utterly serene they always appear to be. In any case, maybe that’s the problem, if/when there ever is one? Surely, some time, at least one of them needs to feel the wind rushing through their metaphorical hair. And what happens then? Having said all that, these two are possibly ideal for each other.

These two should open up a clinic. They could call it, The Just Come Around And Hang Out At Our Place And You’ll Soon Feel Great No Matter What Centre. They probably wouldn’t even charge you, or maybe have a donations box out the front. In a nutshell, these two are good for each other and good for the world. Sure, (2) is the more outgoing of the duo and (9) has a more calming aspect, which both (2) and the world at large appreciates, but there isn’t much going on here which isn’t appreciated. So, we’ll let them go about their rather splendid business while we go about ours. Not much to be worried about here, kids.

What do you get when you put two rather lovely optimists together? You get a great big fluffy happy cake that everyone adores, and that very few people get sick of. Indeed, the only ones who wont like the cake are those classically cynical or antagonistic types who get off on confrontation for the hell of it. Well booo hooo to them!

One imagines Doctor (9) accidentally being seated next to Nurse (2) on the plane, for their flight to Africa, and would any of us be surprised to learn that they’re about to spend the next six months working side by side at the same refuge camp in the Democratic Republic of Congo? In all likelihood, the rest may very well be history, and you definitely don’t need to hear why these two are well suited from us. Equally, don’t ask them. They’ll just get embarrassed, especially (9).

It’s not that these two are interchangeable, but, you know, they could be. Both of them are compassionate and caring souls who tend to make the world a better place, collectively and individually, and the only real hiccup arrives when a hard decision has to be made by someone. Maybe the dog needs to be put down, or maybe there is a grandmother somewhere who is asking to be euthanised? Sounds ridiculous, but life throws up these scenarios and they have to be confronted sooner or later, so, how will these two go? (Actually, we suspect they’ll go very well, but it’ll still be interesting to see how they, or someone, deals with it. Until then though, it’s happy sailing.)

These two are wonderful. They wake up every morning, pull out the day’s agenda (which was decided at least 24hours beforehand) and off they go, diligently ticking off every task with a big grin of satisfaction. And it’s not all just about (1) and (3) either. They want to do good in the world, and this is how they aim to achieve excellence: have a plan directed at their (mutual) goals and bloody well take action to achieve them. 
Too right. 
In fact, is there a more dynamic, target-oriented couple? We’re not sure. 
They talk, they share their problems and behind closed doors they probably have orgasm competitions, at least, we hope this is a distinct possibility.

Watching these two walk out of the building is like watching a successful Prime Minister, (3), stride to the microphone next to a visiting despotic President, (1), whom they happen to be hosting. The speeches are tremendous, broadcast live across the world, and you would never pick that (3) is slightly humoured by the over zealous (1), who, let’s face it, isn’t quite as laid back. Nice to know, however, that it isn’t all about the limelight for these two. Yes, they love the cameras and the barrage of questions fired at them from the press gallery afterwards, but they both really do aim to make their respective countries better places to live in, and they know that they can help each other tremendously. It’s actually just fun to be in the same space as the two of them, and we’re pretty sure prosperity and lower taxes are what’s in store for all of us. “Three cheers for (1) and (3)! Hoorah!”

These two would make wonderful leaders of a cub scout or a girl guide pack, on the proviso that the local newspapers come out and do an article about them. Why? Because each of them seeks to help out and generally do some good, and what better way to be seen to be legendary by society than by helping the youth of the nation! (1) is better at the hands-on details of dealing with kids in canoes, as well as subtly providing general moral guidance, while (3) is far more adept at handling, meeting and greeting visiting photographers, as well as placating worried parents who may have heard a rumour that the lake they are camping at contains crocodiles. Sure, attending large groups of kids requires a lot of energy and at night there is barely any left for these two to be able to share some special intimate time together, but they don’t mind. Most of the kids are happy and, tomorrow, the group photo with these two at the front is going to be on the front page of the paper. Glory!

Is that trumpets we hear in the back ground? By god it is, and here comes Cleopatra, (3), exultant Egyptian leader and goddess, her throne hoisted on the shoulders of mute slaves! What a sight! Oh hang on, and here comes Marc Antony, (1), hoisted in a similar fashion, except he has an entire garrison of the Roman army behind him. What a magnificent sight! 
“Oh, what’s that you say? I can’t hear you for the trumpets…” 
“I said, did you know they’re a couple?”
“Really? Well there you go. They’ll do us proud, won’t they?”
“Yep. He suggested building an aqueduct between Carthage and Alexandria for her, and she agreed to it straight away.”
“Great, but hang on, how do you know that?’
“Cos I’m going to help build it. They’ll even feed us.”
“Ahhh, life is good then.” 
Amen.

These two are good. Think Dave Stewart and Annie Lennox (Eurythmics), think James Watson and Francis Crick (discovered DNA), think Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire (they danced a bit). Do you get the picture? We don’t feel like comparing apples with these two, there’s no real need, suffice to say (1) and (3) are a rather stunning team and they have our congratulations. They’re driven, organised, share a similar goal and in a perfect world they back each other up, being fully aware of the foibles of the other. So, maybe just grab yourself a comfy seat, sit back and watch them do their thing. Too right.

Batman and Robin, eat your heart out, because sometimes some things just work. The only caveat with this wonderful little team is that hopefully the ‘leader’, who in this case is (3), rightly acknowledges their wonderful assistant, (2). If this happens then all will be well, but honestly, they would have to be idiots to mess this relationship up. In many social settings they ooze charm, sexual satisfaction, good humour and happiness. They’re so good, in fact, that on the morning after some giant dinner party or other, while all the guests are at home and having a lazy debrief about the night that was, no one will be able to really discern the difference between either of our wonderful duo. In the memory of these people they’ll just be this delightful, stunning couple-person. Weird, eh?

Most of us are aware of how much of the land settled across the world was achieved by powerful individuals with a sense of adventure and a capacity to get the job done, and to persist in the face of adversity. And that’s great, but how often are these people - yes, we’re talking about you, (3) - propped up and assisted by those around you? We would suggest about 100% of the time, and this is the special skill of (2). But don’t worry, (3) knows this very well and both understand the roles they fulfil when it comes to both getting the sheep ready for shearing as well as looking after the mob of shearers who will attend them. Yep, they’re a fine team, these two.

If you can imagine (3) as James Bond, regardless of their sex, then we would describe (2) as Q, the wonderful, quirky and brilliant technical whizz who gives Bond all the new gadgets, which enables him to do what he does with such success. Are they a splendid team? You’re damn right they are.

This won’t take very long, because today we give you Sherlock and Holmes. That’s right, and you wouldn’t necessarily pick them in these roles, would you? We would. The dashing, charismatic (3) is ideal in their role as the brilliant and gifted sleuth, and they are ably backed up by (2), who is not only no dummy in their own right, but who takes care of important details and often lays the foundation for some wonderful discoveries. Elementary it may be for this couple, but such a pairing doesn’t arrive frequently and all we suggest is that the criminals of the world look out. Bravo!

In actuality, Superman was the foil for Lois Lane, wasn’t he? Lois had the balls and the nous, and sure, Superman had the superpowers, but it was Lois’s pure guts and initiative which drove the whole relationship, and which eventually saved the world. So there you have it. (2) is our wonderful Superman and (3) is the indomitable Lois Lane, and a wonderful duo they are. Roll the credits please.

Possible greatness is in the offing here, no question. If these two have dealt with all their baggage from the past, then they’ll almost certainly move mountains, not only for each other but possibly for the world they live in. That sound silly? Maybe, but these two are into life and making moments count. Alright, yes, they may want to be ‘seen’ and recognised at being remarkable, so there is a collective ego here, but as an old rock band once said, “Ego is not a dirty word.” 
So, kiss whenever and wherever you like and everyone will enjoy the show.

Watching these two is like watching two great tennis players who, together, win all the grand slam events, seemingly alternating between victories. As a couple the only hiccups arise then they need play each other in the final, because as much as they love prevailing, they don’t really want to be beaten by their betrothed. Don’t worry, if one of them doesn’t make the final and the other wins, then no one is cheering louder, but it’s only when they’re involved that things might be momentarily imperfect. Fun duo to watch, no matter what they’re doing.

Welcome to two people who have done the courses, dealt with their baggage and followed their aspirations to a position of now being quite successful in life. Don’t believe us? Don’t care. They enjoy being noticed as being talented or wonderful, be it as a couple or otherwise, and they feel a great sense of (understated) pride to see the other do well, also. (But not so much that only one of them is noticed and never the other.) Sure, they have the capacity to spend way too much at work, or at least, to get so caught up in it that they forget that they might have a mouth or two to feed somewhere, but usually they deal with these responsibilities quite well. When they’re in sync they’re a wonderful team.

Okay, so these two might not sob at the touching movie they’re watching together, but that’s only because they’ve got a mountain of work which needs doing, and it’s hard to get too emotional when you suspect you’re just about to get a paper published in one of the world’s most prestigious scientific journals. This is the life. As far as figuring out if they’re a good couple or not, maybe come back next week after we find out how their submission went. (We suspect they’ll be just fine, although they’ll be tough to get hold of due to the number of interviews being requested of them.)

Watching these two talk is like watching two fighter pilots discuss the ins and outs of the latest war games results, which just finished. Both led their respective squadrons to mock victory though they never actually confronted each other as they happened to be on the same side all the time. Which is actually fine by them. They’d rather not know who was better. But, even if they had faced-off, they’re flying different aircraft anyway and so there would have been an alibi for either of them, had it happened.

Deep, at least this is the theory. If (3) can handle the self-help books, the incense and the heart-felt pieces of advice while (4) stares into their soul from a foot away, then they’ll be okay as a couple. Then again, (3) might prefer to stop (4)’s navel gazing and emotional outpourings, although (3) probably needs the help in opening up. It’s a complicated system, eh? Overall it sounds like it’d be more fun to pour two cups of sand down your underpants and go on a five kilometre run. Good luck!

These two are okay, but (3) is a little disturbed by the fact that (4) seems to get emotoinal whenever they make love. It’s not like (3) doesn’t have a heart, but when compared to the soulful, dramatic nature of (4), maybe they don’t. It’s hard to say. At the very least, if (3) ever wound up ill in hospital (4) would run screaming up the road to get to the them as fast as they could, which would make for wonderful television, in case you’re into that kind of thing. Though we’re not sure what (3) would make of it.

If (3) is the head of the tribe then (4) is the local shaman, and the last thing (3) needs to hear about right now is why stamping a crows foot covered in calf blood on their forehead is going to help make them impervious to injury in tomorrow’s battle. But, (3) doesn’t ever want to hurt (4)’s feelings, and it’s not like (4) doesn’t seem to have an uncanny knack of describing future events quite accurately. So, (3) will do as their told, although, if they make it back tomorrow, they might quietly suggest to (4) that next time, could they please use a fresh batch of blood cos they all stink. (Which, you guessed it, is the only reason (4) did it in the first place because no one likes to fight a stinking adversary.)

In many ways these two are great for each other. (3) aids (4) to express themselves more clearly, primarily by focussing on relevant key points, and (4) helps (3) to get in touch with their deeper feelings and to be more open about heart-felt issues, which even (3) will usually agree they are notoriously crap at. But, if (3) is knee-deep in work and let’s face it, it happens quite a lot, then (4) will feel left out and alone, even more than normal, which, at the same time, might remind (4) that they are going out with a heartless, unromantic workaholic. Good luck!

Here we have (3), the ringleader and disciplinarian in charge of the circus show where they are directing a young elephant, (4), to perform various tricks. The fact that such events occur is something of an anathema, but here we are with a ring-side seat. And just look at little (4) will you? What a cute, adorable creature. All they want is a bit of love, don't they? You can see it. They don't want to roll around like a fool and be laughed at by the crowd. And what of (3)? They look superb in their glittering, tailored suit, and they’re supposed to be famous, but can’t (3) see that all the elephant wants is to be cuddled and not made fun of? What happens when the elephant grows up?

No time for laziness here folks. No way. In a perfect world, the brilliant and dispassionate analytical skills of our NASA scientist, (5), are of tremendous help to the more flamboyant Launch Manager, (3). Likewise, the pizazz of (3)’s influence can be a tremendous addition to (5)’s philosophical/psychological quiver. In many ways (3) sees (5) as some kind of burrowing genius who just needs to be pointed in the right direction, which, in some cases, (5) might take quite personally. One proviso: If they begin competing with each other they’re screwed.

Never a dull moment with some couples, is there? There is no questioning (5)’s capacity to invent and to explore, and if ever they needed a good PR person then (3) would do a great job, although usually (3) has their own successful career to worry about. If they turn each other on then they’d have a grand old time in bed, but even outside the bedroom each provides the other with enough mental stimulation to keep everyone happy and enthused.

Like a fine and potentially expensive wine, these two definitely improve with age, mostly because both of them, in their own ways, are deep thinkers who can plan ahead and who realise moment-to-moment glory is largely a myth. And it helps too if they are not only recognised as being skilled and brilliant by each other, but also by those around them. We imagine the only real hiccup for (5) and (3), aside from potentially over-working, is if one person starts to let the team down by suddenly proving to be mediocre. But that’s not going to happen, right?

As an otter who has just constructed their best dam yet, (5) is constantly seeking to improve and to learn new ways of doing things. And while they secretly love the adulation from (3), who sat on the sidelines the whole while and offered small but pivotal pieces of advice whenever they saw fit, they won’t readily admit it. (3) on the other hand, kept reminding (5) that if they happened to come across a small crustacean during construction to grab it and toss it their direction for later, which (5) duly did. So, yes, they’re a fine if not slightly dysfunctional team, and we look forward to seeing how the dam holds up. Splendid.

Does (3) ever become somewhat disheartened by (5)’s apparent lack of compassion? Well, yes they do, but overall they’ve learnt not to take it personally. Likewise, (5) is accustom to (3)’s occasional emotional outbursts which tend to be funny rather than diabolical. In their eyes at least, anyway. What we have here is a highly functional pair of humans whose depths are far more intricate than what any of us might see on the surface. Maybe don’t ask (5) their opinion on how they are going - for things in their world either are or they aren't - but so far (3) is a pretty happy camper. And there’s our (current) answer.

Here we have an event rarely seen in the wild, an Alsatian paired with an anxious but excitable Cocker Spaniel. At least they’re the same species, give or take, because they have plenty in common. The Alsatian, (3), is keen to get ahead, to complete the mission, to look good while it’s happening and to ultimately succeed by finding and devouring that hidden bone. Our Cocker Spaniel however, (6), is far more social and definitely more easily distracted. Make no mistake, (6) loves finding a hidden bone just as much as the next hound but their approach is vastly different, that’s all.
