Frustrations may appear from both sides but if they can manage to fluke getting a bone together then they might be okay.

Theoretically, these two are doing alright, but there are differences. For instance, if (3) and (6) are late to get to a wedding and (6) spies an injured animal by the side of the road, or perhaps an especially miserable-looking homeless person, then they will most likely insist (3) stop the car so they can both help somehow. True, this isn’t necessarily a bad thing for (3) - we all need to be compassionate for those who are suffering - and while (3) generally likes the fact (6) stands up for the less fortunate way more than they do, right now they need to be somewhere and this isn’t helping. But, (3) will do the right thing today, and they’ll be even later in arriving, however, if (6) pulls a similar stunt on the way home the shit will definitely hit the fan.

Yep, (3) is naturally more confident and self-assured than (6), and (6) can be a terrific support, although they are no slouch at working hard and achieving goals, either. Usually, (3) is more dynamic out there in the world, although (6) has a better grasp on some of life’s realities. Is the car due for a service? When can we get someone in to take care of the mould underneath these awnings? Can we organise someone to come and clip the dog’s claws? - these kinds of questions aren’t really on (3)’s radar, and usually they don’t mind stepping up once asked. It’s when (3) starts to repeatedly forget to do something that problems begin to fester and insecurities here seem to pile up quite quickly.

Listen, if (6) ever starts taking (3)’s directives too personally, and it happens repeatedly, then the whole shebang will come crashing down in a heap in a matter of days. So (3), if you care about (6) just take half a second to analyse your words before they come out of your mouth. Yeah, yeah, we know - that’s tough, but it’s not beyond you and (6) is worth it, and they’re probably not quite as sensitive as we’re leading you to believe. So, a little gentleness here goes a long way. It’s your perceived arrogance, (3), that’s getting (6) worked up, so siddown and take a chill pill.

Do you ever lie back and marvel at the notion of why and how we just don’t all get along, having made the decision to be with someone? We don’t get it - don’t understand how so many people make a decision of their own volition, yet end up bickering and fighting and being disrespectful, and not acting with love as their purest intention. How did this come to be? We’re bloody sick of it, just now. Are you paying attention to (6)’s moods, (3)? Do you not understand that they’ll never be as driven as you? And do you (6) realise it’s your job to help (3) become a little more humane and compassionate? And it’s their job to bloody take heed of this. So, don’t freak out when (3) acts like a sanctimonious, arrogant pain in the arse. They’re trying to do their job and you are trying to do yours. Right. Good night.

Watching (3) and (7) is exhausting enough, and we certainly can’t imagine what it’s like actually being in the relationship. Like watching the formation of a new star or some such phenomena, the amount of noise, light and heat generated by these two means that we, as observers, probably need to bring sedatives, a good chair, sunglasses and definitely some water to cool us down. These two never sit still and their arguments can be highly entertaining, especially for each other. Together they are kids at heart and if, heaven forbid, someone gets seriously hurt or offended then the ending will be swift and they’ll hopefully forget about each other, soon enough.

These two are a riot. And most likely famous. How they stay together is largely beyond us because they attract so much energy and brilliance that surely someone’s head is likely to just pop off one night, mostly out of pure excitement. We’re not kidding. As usual, (3) often has to do the apologising or explaining after (7) has accidentally destroyed something expensive in someone’s house, but what do you do? According to (7), if nothing is destroyed during a party then it’s not a  party. The only issue, if they have one, is that (3) will always work harder and dedicate more time to their career. (7), as you might expect, goes out of their way to avoid the use of such terms altogether. Anyway, they’ll be fine.

(3) has tried explaining to (7) that they can’t just blurt out what they’re thinking any time they feel like it. 
“Did I offend someone?” (7) will ask, genuinely surprised.
“(7), did you not see the look on his face when you reminded his partner that you slept with them, back in Chicago?”
“Oh shit, did I say that?”
(3) shakes their head. “Listen, I don’t care who you slept with, you know that, but can you just try and take a second next time. I was embarrassed for him.”
(7) smiles and says, “Well, yeah, okay…but you have to admit it was pretty funny, eh? If I really said that, I mean.”
“It was bloody hilarious (7), but that’s not the point!”

And then they probably went and had some ‘pretend make up sex’ just for the hell of it.

These two can achieve just about anything. At their best they could make themselves famous, or at least one of them anyway, if they’re hunting that type of thing. They attract people and events and are, generally speaking, larger than life. At their worst, which doesn’t seem to happen too frequently, they’ve been known to set entire apartment blocks on fire, crimes of passion have happened, cars have been wrecked and insurance companies have wanted them killed. But as we say, this is in no way the norm. (3) and (7) have the capacity to be utterly brilliant, and we’ll be watching them closely.

It's lucky they have a budget to work with because in each other’s company neither of them is any good at saying the word NO. In fact, that about sums these two up. Last we heard they were sailing a yacht through Greece, but at (7)’s insistence, so the rumour goes, (3) agreed to see if they could sail all the way to New York. Anyone know if they’ve arrived yet? Hold on, hold on, is this story bullshit or is it legit? Oh wait! No way! (3) has just sent us a text……

Oh my god….you’re not going to believe what’s happened! 

(Moral to the story: (3) and (7) are a grand, life changing duo. The end.)

And suddenly we are confronted with the two drivers from a Formula 1 racing team. Yes, technically they’re on the same side, but the head driver, (8), is far more demonstrative and confrontational than (3). Don’t worry, they bring the best out in each other, but they sometimes forget that they’re trying to win the Driver’s Championship for the team, together. If they get too deep into the interpersonal rivalry then someone will begin insisting that the other driver isn’t supporting them. If this goes on for very long and isn’t dealt with then there’ll be nothing team management can do, and we might even see fisticuffs in pit lane. Either way, it’ll make for excellent television, so keep watching…

First things first - (8), pull your head in for a second. You’re not the only person who matters in this relationship. Yes, you are charismatic and usually right, but (3) is too, and they are a powerful personality in their own right. Sure, they may not love confrontation like you (8), but not many people do. So if you can just sit down for a second and shut up, we’d like to hear what (3) has to say on the issue, and we will not stand for interruptions. (By the way, we only said 10% compatibility in order to get you both thinking. Good luck!)

Okay, so we all know how (8) can act like Julius Caesar on a bad day. Luckily, (3) is no slouch and not the push-over (8) usually enjoys trying to manipulate. Yes (8), we think you’re something of a control freak, who enjoys pushing peoples’ buttons. Your issue (3) is that if you don’t lavish the right amount of attention in (8)’s direction they’ll spit the dummy anyway. Sounds complicated, huh? Anyway, you probably know this already (3) but don’t let (8) get away with too much. Half the time they’re just seeing what your limits are. You are used to excelling (3) and you’ll work them out. Buon chance!

If (3) is the successful jockey with a stellar career behind them, then (8) is the tempestuous mare who loves nothing more than trying to break a bone somewhere on their rider’s body, just to show who’s really in charge. This clashing of heads when it happens makes for splendid viewing whether they win any races or not, and to be honest, we’re not sure they will. If they can manage to listen to each other, maybe tone down their respective egos just a little, then it’s possible these two could achieve unmitigated greatness. We just don’t know, so don’t let our % estimate put you off, it’s just that, if you’re not in sync and not appreciating each others’ endeavours, you might have to get past the notion that, at some point, each of you will feel like you’re sleeping with the enemy. As ever, good luck!

And here we have another despotic leader, (8), who takes a refusal of their suggestions very badly, where as (3), the rather more humble yet equally capable Minister of Foreign Affairs, seems to spend most of their time, not concerning themselves with their own expansive and time consuming portfolio, but placating visiting dignitaries who (8) has offended, again. And we’re just about sick of this, if fact the whole population is. You figure it out (3) but if you decide to quite parliament you have our blessing. Amen.

It’s as if we’re watching a sitcom. The high-powered, fretting fool, (3), trots out the door to work with humble aspirations of being incredibly industrious, generally dazzling, semi-famous and perhaps even world-changing. Later in the day they arrive home stressed and bothered, which is where our host of the century, (9), gets to tend our strident wannabe. Luckily, at home, they desire similar things in life and, yes, (9) admires (3)’s world conquering attitude, but don’t worry, this isn’t all one-way traffic. (3) admires (9)’s capacity to remain calm and their skill at producing a constant, warm interaction because they know they need the help. They might do okay, these two.

Now we’re talking. The potent bulldozer (3) in concert with the gentle and loving landscaper (9), who darts around them with daisies in their hair, removing vulnerable animals, offering water and sandwiches to the bulldozer driver, and generally making sure no one and nothing is being accidentally run over and/or killed. And (9) also takes photographs of (3)’s wonderful work so they can post them on social media later, because (3) secretly loves the adulation. Yes, it’s a little asinine for (3) to need this but so what, no one is perfect although these two aren’t far off it.

What do you get when you cross a potent leader and general go-getter, (3), with lovely warm magical glove, (9), who imparts the wearer with serene superpowers of optimism, loveliness and serenity? That’s right, you get the most wonderful and stress-free ride down the mountain side, that is so fun and tremendous you can’t really imagine doing anything else for the rest of the day. The End.

It’s not that (9) is lazy, it’s just that they operate on a slower tic, and so (3) can always help them get parts of their life in order, if indeed they require any of that. Maybe (9) needs their tax receipts organised? Maybe they even need to learn why or how keeping tax receipts is theoretically important in the first place? Anyway, as silly as some of these concepts are to (9) in the grand scheme of things, (3) is a diligent and competent cat who grasps most administrative systems very well, and who enjoys helping out when they have a few minutes free. Ditto, (9) might just help (3) relax and to appreciate the finer things in life which money can rarely buy.

Ain’t no car wrecks here folks. No smashed vases thrown against a kitchen wall. No divots above the TV where a high velocity potato has met its doom. No sugar-filled petrol tanks in anyone’s car. These two are a nice mix of power and pragmatism, as displayed by (3), and stability, humility and calm, as exemplified by (9). So only a couple of questions remain: are they getting married, and are you invited?

Like an open-minded Nazi, (1), who has fallen in love with a psychic and practicing Buddhist, (4), these two might be a tremendous pairing purely because of the differences of philosophy they each bring, but it will take a lot of work to get the relationship functioning smoothly. (4) is into navel gazing and intimacy-craving, whereas (1) is into getting themselves organised and working hard. Can it work? Well, of course, but we’re climbing a mountain here kiddies and you’ll need to be prepared for the inevitable run of bad weather. We suggest you don’t give up until someone suddenly isn’t there any more. In fact, you know what.....aah, actually, don't worry about it.

We know that any combination of two people has the capacity to work, but this one really is more problematic than most. Why? Because getting anything done here is like observing a financial manager, (1), home from a busy day at the office, attempt and locate and book a table at an appropriate restaurant for (4), who is adamant that the feng shui be just right, and not just any restaurant will do. And it seems most scenarios in their lives butt up against this disparity of life-approaches. (4) will get frustrated that (1) doesn’t understand their point of view and (1) will be saddened that they two of them can never seem to do anything smoothly. Our advice? Just don’t!

Cats: they’re a fascinating creature, but have you ever tried to shoo a group of them over to one part of the room, or perhaps endeavoured to heard them towards a doorway? That’s right, its bloody impossible, and this is the dilemma faced by these two. As a staunchly independent and free-thinking soul, and as brilliant as they occasionally are, (4) has a hard time not doing what they please and certainly expressing how they feel, whenever they want, and they definitely resent being badgered into anything. (1) on the other hand has morals and self-discipline, and doesn’t mind adhering to a plan if that is what was agreed upon earlier. So, how to solve this little conundrum?

Day one of the ski trip - (4)’s idea - and (1) is ready early: goggles and helmet on, appropriate jacket, trousers and gloves on, lifts passes in pocket, skis at the ready, bottle of water and sandwich tucked away. 
“Okay, let’s go,” (1) says, about to blast out the door.
“Just a minute,” (4) replies. “I’m nearly ready, but can we go to the run at the other side of the mountain?”
“What are you talking about?” asks (1). “Isn’t this where you wanted to start?”
“I know,” says (4), “but I think we might better off on the other side.
“Why do you say that? You were here last year! This is why we came here? And you’re a better skier than me!”

Indeed, this kind of thing seems to happen whenever they do anything together.

Yes, there is a touch of oil and water about these two. (4) is like a wild horse who likes to run with the breeze through their mane, galloping over mountain and through rivers with gay abandon, and going where the winds and the seasons direct them, bounded by nothing. (1) on the other hand may very well have a touch of OCD about them, in that they strive for perfection, abhor chaos and the unknown, and find a great deal of pleasure in walking back in the front door to discover the house in perfect order. So, you tell us, how do you think they’ll go when aiming at any kind of relationship? Our advice? If you’re matched sexually, knock yourselves out and have a fab time, but go your separate ways after breakfast.

Page one, line one: talk to each other, you two. 
Spill your guts about everything. Shine a torch into every dark cranny and spit it all out. Leave no stone unturned. Do you hear? Now read that again (2) and (4), aloud this time. In fact, keep reading it otherwise you’ll slip back into old habits and forget everything. Flush out all your insecurities and expose them to the light. Indeed, it’s probably good advice for all of us, but you two need it if you are going to survive because neediness is a useful asset for no one. 
Do that, then come back and here and we’ll have a look at you.

Here we have a social worker going out with a psychotherapist. On paper this should work, right? But perhaps the latter, (4), is just a bit too deep and intense for our more fluid and streetwise (2). Theory is important and things need to be discussed, sure, and lord knows (4)’s couch is comfortable, but at some point these theories have to move from the salon to the real world. Let us know how you get on, and remember to retain a sense of humour at all times, but being friends might be nice, eh?

Like a theoretical physicist who sets foot in a working observatory for the first time, (4) might find the reality of this remarkable piece of engineering quite daunting. The chief researcher at the facility, (2), has seen this reaction before and they are accustom to the look of fear. It’s a pretty impressive telescope, that’s for sure, and (2) is very proud of it, not to mention what it can do. But if (4) requires days of reassurance about the calculations they’ve arrived at, with regards to this star they are supposed to be studying, by the time they get to turn the telescope at the particular sun in question the whole sky would have shifted and it’ll be too late. So, what to do? We don’t know. Maybe go back and re-calibrate for twelve years into the future.

Once again we have an issue on the work site. Our resident environmentalist and bird-lover, (4), is standing in front of a large tree which, (2), head of town planning, needs to cut down. They don’t want to cut it down, really, and all they’re trying to do is stop the local cyclists from being killed by a falling limb, which is inevitable because the tree is now truly old, and the council can’t afford to be sued. So, (2) has no choice but to listen to (4), who sensitivity on this issue knows no bounds, but what can they do? Yes, they’ve tried explaining about saving cyclists’ lives and all (4) does is start ranting about how there are too many people on the planet. And round and round we go. Is anyone else sick of this argument?

And here we have the renowned, reclusive artist, (4), humorous on the surface and definitely talented, chatting to the owner of the local art gallery, (2), who loves showcasing as many local artists as they can. Obviously, (2) is way more social than (4), and they’re very aware that catering to the various needs of some artists is an exercise in diplomacy, almost, no matter how much they love their work. And it seems this is what might be developing here. (4) is quirky and brilliant, no question, but (2) is in a bind  because while they don’t have the resources to demarcate an entire section of the gallery to (4)’s work, they desperately want it hanging in the gallery. How do they solve this issue? Anyone?

Deep, at least this is the theory. If (3) can handle the self-help books, the incense and the heart-felt pieces of advice while (4) stares into their soul from a foot away, then they’ll be okay as a couple. Then again, (3) might prefer to stop (4)’s navel gazing and emotional outpourings, although (3) probably needs the help in opening up. It’s a complicated system, eh? Overall it sounds like it’d be more fun to pour two cups of sand down your underpants and go on a five kilometre run. Good luck!

These two are okay, but (3) is a little disturbed by the fact that (4) seems to get emotoinal whenever they make love. It’s not like (3) doesn’t have a heart, but when compared to the soulful, dramatic nature of (4), maybe they don’t. It’s hard to say. At the very least, if (3) ever wound up ill in hospital (4) would run screaming up the road to get to the them as fast as they could, which would make for wonderful television, in case you’re into that kind of thing. Though we’re not sure what (3) would make of it.

If (3) is the head of the tribe then (4) is the local shaman, and the last thing (3) needs to hear about right now is why stamping a crows foot covered in calf blood on their forehead is going to help make them impervious to injury in tomorrow’s battle. But, (3) doesn’t ever want to hurt (4)’s feelings, and it’s not like (4) doesn’t seem to have an uncanny knack of describing future events quite accurately. So, (3) will do as their told, although, if they make it back tomorrow, they might quietly suggest to (4) that next time, could they please use a fresh batch of blood cos they all stink. (Which, you guessed it, is the only reason (4) did it in the first place because no one likes to fight a stinking adversary.)

In many ways these two are great for each other. (3) aids (4) to express themselves more clearly, primarily by focussing on relevant key points, and (4) helps (3) to get in touch with their deeper feelings and to be more open about heart-felt issues, which even (3) will usually agree they are notoriously crap at. But, if (3) is knee-deep in work and let’s face it, it happens quite a lot, then (4) will feel left out and alone, even more than normal, which, at the same time, might remind (4) that they are going out with a heartless, unromantic workaholic. Good luck!

Here we have (3), the ringleader and disciplinarian in charge of the circus show where they are directing a young elephant, (4), to perform various tricks. The fact that such events occur is something of an anathema, but here we are with a ring-side seat. And just look at little (4) will you? What a cute, adorable creature. All they want is a bit of love, don't they? You can see it. They don't want to roll around like a fool and be laughed at by the crowd. And what of (3)? They look superb in their glittering, tailored suit, and they’re supposed to be famous, but can’t (3) see that all the elephant wants is to be cuddled and not made fun of? What happens when the elephant grows up?

On paper, you might imagine that these two are potentially ideal for one another because both of them love talking and teasing apart life’s respective tragedies and joys, the tragedies especially. They’ll spend days and days analysing their childhoods and explaining any modern-day gripes they have (or perceive they have) with one another, meanwhile the sun outside is glorious and inviting, and they’ve already knocked back an invite from friends who suggested they come on an adventure to a waterfall. 
Perhaps we can’t blame them. After all, why do that when they can sit around inside and study your emotional baggage? They’re like a Mills and Boon novel, but can they save one another? Are they happy? Good! But for anyone outside, it’s like watching paint dry.

Mmmm, will they get on each other’s nerves eventually? That’s a fine question. Let’s go and see what they’re up to, shall we? Now, there they are in the meditation room and they’ve only been there for six hours, sitting cross-legged in front of each other, gazing into each other’s eyes, palms pressed against one another’s. Are they talking? No, but they must be communicating, don’t you think? I guess. Shall we knock and ask what they’re doing. SHIT NO! STOP! DON’T DISTURB THEM. Okay, okay, jeepers. We’ll just leave them to it, shall we? Yep, that’s a good idea, let’s come back tomorrow.

Are they sexually well-matched, does anyone know?……No one knows? Okay, well, we imagine they might be, but probably only in the realm of tantric sex because this is the most spiritually intense and emotional, and it takes the longest. Which means, theoretically, they are a good match, right? Are they just too similar, we wonder? They can’t be needing to soul-search 24/7 can they, surely not?

These two are like a pair of Emperor penguins reuniting after the female has just spent three months at sea, and who is returning to find herself with a fresh new chick. They squark and slap each other, putting on an elaborate display, which is the key to reminding each other that they have the right penguin. Except this pair, as humans, do this every time they walk in the bloody door as a means to reinforce their bond. Someone should make a documentary about them. As far as being a suitable life match, at least for this breeding season, we’ll say yes, but penguins don’t mate for life you know. That’s all bullshit.

Like a couple of psychics who have just met and who are both convinced they were lovers in a past life, they are ‘in tune’ with each other. If you’re not a fan of public displays of affection then these two might get on your nerves. We love it, but when these two are all loved-up, everyone around them feels like they’re invisible. So, we wish them well, and the only concerns arise are when they are confronted with a major, real-world issue to contend with. If aliens arrive with a mission to wipe us all out, for instance, these two might discover that a pack of taro cards will only hold out for so long against a high-powered, nucleated laser beam. But, as ever, it will make for splendid viewing pleasure.

At best, these two produce a long, in-depth team meeting and both of them have plenty to talk about. In the case of their respective brains functioning the same way, this would be great. However, we are confronted with two diametrically opposed personalities. (5), arguably the most clinical observer in the animal kingdom, very quickly becomes either bored or frustrated at how (4) constantly wants to talk about how they feel and what upsets them. Conversely, (4) is usually in a perpetual state of disbelief at how uncaring (5) seems to be. And don’t get (4) started on (5)’s apparent lack of intimacy and affection, heavens to mercy! We could be here all night.

(4) is the artist.
(5) is the scientist.
(4) is the campfire.
(5) is the bunsen burner.
(4) is the writer.
(5) is the editor, critic and publisher.
(4) lives largely inside themselves (to a large extent).
(5) almost never does (to a large extent). 
(4) needs deep connections.
(5) observes how or why deep connections are important. 
Are they good people?
Yes.
Are they a perfect match?
Mmmm…

(4)'s greatest wish for their partner is that they could unzip (5)’s head, pull out their brain, put it on for twenty minutes and see what they are really thinking or feeling. No, (5) isn’t the best at discussing these things, but only because on a list of priorities, pulling apart their deepest fears, hopes and emotions is somewhere near the bottom. Does this difference bode well for a long-lasting, close-knit relationship? We tend to think no, but, bless us all, humans are a weird and wonderful bunch and you just never know till you give it a try. Good luck!

Perhaps the largest hurdle for these two is for (5) not to become overwhelmed by (4)’s emotional intensity. In which case, does that mean they both have to act in a way which isn’t natural? Perhaps, then again maybe they just need to do that only a little, and get a bit of practice at it. In (5)’s case, maybe try not to mock a crazy idea as soon as (4) mentions it, or at least compliment them on one aspect of it before you pour cold water on it. And (4), if that happens, take the compliment, accept that (5) is trying to be considerate, but definitely don’t take any ensuing criticism personally. Remember (4), you and you alone are responsible for your happiness, and yep, that goes for everyone. Amen.

Can we look at that again in slow motion? Here we see (5) slowly turn back to the sink where they are in the middle of doing the dishes, having just whimsically suggested to (4), who is sitting at the kitchen table behind them, that they only watch television because they don’t have any meaningful hobbies in their life. Now, see the furrows of anger appear quite quickly on (4)’s forehead, as they instinctively snatch at their cup of water. (4) then hurls the cup at (5)’s back, and the vision of the water ejecting from the cup in slow motion on it’s way to impact is just brilliant. And then, here we see the shock of (5)’s body as water and cup crash into the back of them…..What a lovely, joyous morning.

Have you ever seen footage of two snakes engaged in coitus? You don’t know which snake is which, and here in a modern, human coupling we might be observing something very similar. Are (4) and (6) perfectly suited - the answer is a resounding YES! Talk about a match made in heaven, especially if each of them has already sorted out their emotional carry-on luggage. Then again, it probably doesn’t matter because, regardless, quite quickly each of them will feel like they are going out with their own private, brilliant psychiatrist. Perfect! The only issue, which is ours, is that if you are a friend of theirs then you might need to start looking around for some others.

Righto, who has the popcorn? These two are good. Do they both feel a little bit lost? Well not any more because finally each has met a like-minded soul, willing to bare all as a means to get to their own respective truths. Turns out both of them are loveable after all, although we could have told you that ages ago you pair of fools! In fact, that’s enough from us and we’ll leave it at that. Bravo! We’ll see you later, and if you decide to fill out all those forms and tick all those societal driven boxes, we’d love an invite to the wedding. Cheers.

Looking at (4) and (6) together is like looking at one of those pictures where someone is giving a giant eagle a hug, and where the eagle has their wings out and is hugging the human right back. Crazy, eh? You could say it’s corny but it’s also pretty remarkable. Maybe we’re just envious, but that looks like fun. Keep up the good work and we’ve nothing more to add.

These two are a fine pairing, and the only hiccup - well, one of the only hiccups - arises when or if (4) suggests to (6) that they try out the new nude beach. (6) isn’t necessarily as free-wheeling as (4), so this kind of suggestion might take them a little getting used to, but it’s a first world problem in our eyes. These kinds of suggestions is why (6) is with (4) in the first place. So, shall we just pop down the beach with our binoculars and see how they go?….Wicked!

Like a light in the dark, is how both (4) and (6) might describe their meeting each other. And how often does someone suggest something like that of their partner? That’s right, not very bloody often. True, they are a couple of hopeless romantics, (4) especially, and so they’re allowed the odd grandiose statement. Indeed, it’s quite refreshing in the modern era, where people toss around words like ‘awesome’ and ‘epic’ like throw-away confetti. Anyway, there is a real potential bond here that might very well last longer than just this summer. And bully for them if it does.

Unless these two are heavily into BDSM, or a have a fetish for Chinese riverboats, or perhaps they developed a penchant training and flying pigeons, they are screwed. They’re just too different. (7) craves the wind through their hair and miles and miles of paddocks to run across, naked, preferably,  while (4) dotes on the idea of rubbing each others’ fingernails in the morning with that special someone, whispering little secrets. 
Yes, we’re talking chalk and cheese. We’re talking flashlights and watermelons. We’re talking suspenders on a cactus plant. 
Forget the whole thing.

(7) staggers in the door, smelling of booze and with a twisted smile on their face, having hardly slept for two days, to discover (4) standing next to an intimate looking table-for-two in the dining room, which they prepared two nights ago.
“…Uh oh,” (7) says, after they get their bearings.
“Yep. Uh oh is right,” replies (4).

And there endeth the lesson.

Like a determined, loving and usually-forgiving Tibetan monk, (4), holding on to the tail of a Bengal tiger, (7), who is desperate to get some food or fun into their gob, there is a reasonable probability that if the tiger isn’t sated soon, they’ll just turn around and eat the monk. Not out of malice, mind you. (7) is just hungry, and perhaps a little bored, and (4) just happens to be the nearest option.

“Hey, do you want to go see that band, tonight?” asks (7), sticking their head around the corner into the bathroom.
“Um, well I thought we could stay in,” replies (4). “There’s a couple of things I want to talk to you about. Plus we haven’t eaten at home for ages.”
(7) looks surprised. “Oh, okay. We’ve got five minutes now. What’s up?”
“Well, no, can’t we have a nice dinner together? It might take a while.”
“Alright,” (7) sighs. “I’ll be back by six. If we’re eating early it means we’ll have time for the band. I’ll just go downtown and get the tickets. See you soon.”
Before (4) can complain (7) has vanished out the door, which gives them plenty of time to wonder how long they can do this for.

If (4) is the rather gentle and gifted nature photographer then (7) is a Viking chieftain, and it would seem one of them has been transported either forward or back in time to a place in which they may not survive very long. Certainly, we don’t expect them to cope too well together, although (7) would make a tremendous subject for (4), and god knows that if (7) is going to survive in the modern world they’ll need some advice on how to behave. It might be a short-run thing but it might be fun to watch, eh?

Wow, you ready? 
When these two are good they’re incredible. They generate more sexual heat, philosophical fun and intrigue, and more overall passion than almost any duo. (8) is larger than life and inspires all those in their midst, which is terribly exciting for a wee homebody like (4). Ditto, (4) is incredibly insightful and more attuned to people’s energy, which is something (8) can really learn and benefit from.
On the flip-side, if things go to shit – i.e. (8) becomes too loud and aggressive or (4) becomes too demanding and sensitive - then you won’t find a more pathetic, bitchy, petty, quibbling couple of painful, whinging shit-heads. Who knows, maybe they actually like it that way? I guess we’ll find out…

Yep, nice. The world champion platform diver, (8), known and famed around the planet for their daredevil leaps of death-defying brilliance, and whose very core is lit-up by operating on the razor’s edge, is nurtured and propelled by their loving mentor and sage, (4), who has come to know exactly how to encourage an abet their supreme athlete. What a wonderful sight! Yes, Redbull pays for everything and no one goes home unhappy, least of all these two.

The truth: this is what these two are skilled at looking for and talking about. Yes, (8)’s approach is akin to a bull hunting for brilliance in a china shop where as (4)’s is more like trying to coax out a kitten from beneath a massive sofa bed, but at least they’re on the same page. Sexually, who knows, but relationshipically they’re a damn fine match and, certainly, (4) finds (8) a simply startling prospect who will help them break out of their shell, if indeed one exists. (8) is just happy for the encouraging audience who generally appreciates what they’re on about.

(8) is the daring acrobatic pilot and (4) is their engineer who is extremely sensitive to every sound and vibration the aircraft makes. (8) hasn’t got the attention span to deal with specifics like hydraulic pressure and oil temperature, they’re just good at flying and putting on a wonderful show. Will they crash? Not if (4) has anything to do with it. And while (8) scares the willies out of (4), there is no place either of them would rather be. Sweet!

Not often does (8) come up against someone who matches their natural desire to get to the bottom of things, and to discover what is really going on. (4) not only does that very well, but they challenge (8) regularly on an emotional level, which is unusual, and part of the reason (8) finds (4) so intriguing and wonderful. They’re actually lucky to have each other, and in all likelihood, so are we because it means we can all relax and let someone else field all thier questiions. Amen.

Respectively, (4) and (9) are on a fervent search for that soul mate who they feel ‘completes them’. Is that a corny load of unmitigated bullshit?… probably, but as it stands they might be on the right track. They’re definitely more likely to lounge around all day together rather than leap out of bed at dawn, don the matching lycra and hit the running track or the freezing beach swim. Fluffy pillows, tea and toast in bed, big long talks and gentle caresses are what’s on offer here ladies and gentlemen. 
Bored yet? They probably feed each other in restaurants, who knows. But, perhaps that lack of pure energy is what irks them in the end, if it happens.

No, we’re not in the presence of two professional pole dancers, but two professional bird-watchers who, in a perfect world, get to enjoy their ornithological pursuits while at the same time rubbing shoulders with each other. One might argue that it’s not even the birds they’re interested in, but the necessarily quiet and peaceful places they have to hide together while they list down, and occasionally photograph, their quarry. And they get to whisper to each other, which they like doing as well. Yep, it’s all good for these two.

Yes, another loving, romantic soup in the brewing here kiddies, and why not indeed! Both crave that intimate connection where feelings are shared, partners are encouraged and acts of romance are commonplace. Nice work if you can get it, right? On a bad day (9) will shut up shop and not feel like talking about anything, which has a tendency to really piss (4) off, where as (9) might be bothered by (4)’s absurd mood swings, although we suspect this is a rarity more than the norm. Shall we all take a seat and just see how they get on?….Wonderful.

Does (4) provide enough oomph for (9), and does (9) allow and encourage (4) to express themselves fully? The answer, most of the time, is a resounding yes. Maybe it's the artistic, emotional streak they both share - we don’t know, but we like it. Are they shagging much, does anyone know?….Anyway, we look forward to the update ladies and gentlemen and unless there is some major disaster or other, you probably won’t see these two for a while, such is their propensity for lazing all over each other in front of Netflix.

What? A renegade couple deliberately crashed a car into the local ATM, shot two police officers and high-tailed it across the border? Well good on them, but in a billion, actually, in ten billion years you are never going to see (4) and (9) do that. Hell, the only time these two move quickly is to dash for the kitchen after the microwave beeps to let them know their hot chocolates are ready, and they’re not shy on the cocoa sprinkled on top, either. Somehow it makes their little cubby hut that they have going in the lounge room more romantic. Yeah, I know, we don’t get it either. We’ve stopped asking, but so what, they’re happy and that’s what counts.

Like two highly intelligent and inquisitive creatures hailing from different planets altogether, their respective aims and desires are ostensibly the same, it’s just that the nuances of language, and therefore perceived intent, take a long time to coincide. Both are highly curious and analysing their environment is something they appear to be well-developed for. And they have a sense of humour, though (5) is far more adept at dealing with the unknown than (1). 
And, to be honest, (5) occasionally deliberately provides a little chaos, just to see what will happen. It’s a good way to test a hypothesis, though this often angers (1), and this is but one of many mis-communications.

These two are like the sorcerer and the apprentice. Yes, magic looks like a lot of mystical wonderment, but in actual fact it’s all just physics and momentum undertaken with deftness, nonchalance and speed. Our sorcerer, (5), whose face one rarely sees, knows all the tricks, is ruffled by very little, be it a poor audience reaction or a slightly slashed belly, and is constantly on the look out for new and high quality acts which they can use as part of his or her show. (1) on the other hand is doing very well to keep up, and they have a few tricks of their own, although their capacity to absorb the unexpected into their routine might require some attention, and we’re not sure if this is something that can be taught or not. Maybe the same stage isn’t something these two should be considering? But, they definitely put on a good show, at least for a short while.

(5) is like the unseen union mastermind who doesn’t mind receiving the odd bribe, if only for the fact that the entire system is corrupt and true altruism, they know, will only bring dissatisfaction, and a failure to achieve anything meaningful. (1) on the other hand has just left university and regularly marches in protest - workers’ rights, land rights, the environment, etc etc - and they were delighted to join the union with the hope of making a real difference to the poor and downtrodden of the world. What is (5) to do? They know the truth of the system will kill (1), but not to tell them will only destroy them in the long run, which is probably worse. So they have no choice. Hence, in terms of a relationship, is disappointment inevitable? If (1) is strong, smart and flexible enough, not necessarily.

If you imagine (1) as the young race car driver who is newly arrived into the team, and who carries a reputation, then (5) is the head mechanic who knows the ins and outs of this car better than anyone. Sure, (1) is the soul who sits behind the wheel and risks life and limb to race the thing, but (5) can tell exactly how it’s being driven and knows precisely how it can be driven better. This is cutting edge technology we’re talking about and the computers don’t lie, neither does the amount of wear on the cylinders and the tyres, and while (5) listens intently to what (1) has to say with regards to handling and general feel - they’re not totally stupid - at the end of the day this young hoon, skilled though they are, is still extremely naive as to what this machine is capable of. So, I guess we’ll sit down and watch the race, eh? There’s bound to be a crash some time…

Ever seen the British TV show, Yes Minister? It’s old, true, but is it the funniest, most relevant political show ever made? It must be close. Anyway, if one imagines (1) as the high-minded politician who needs to be seen to be doing the right thing, and to hopefully adhere to set of morals which can be both useful and admired, then (5) is their chief advisor who knows very well the entire system is a bloody farce, and that providing a facade which appears to be intact, conscientious and transparent is vital if the government is to remain in power, and, to a lesser extent, appear to be seen to actually try and achieve something meaningful. No, (1) is not a puppet at the hands of (5) but there are certain inalienable truths which need to be told, but only at the right time, and only if required. Plausible deniability is something (1) simply doesn’t need to know about. So, marriage here?….Mmmm….not so sure.

What have we got here? A quick-run thing or a crack at long-term love and greatness? If it’s the former we’ve no suggestions - you’ll work out the opposing mysteries one way or the other soon enough - but if it’s the latter then you both need to get out your geological survey equipment. You’ll need your night goggles, make sure your first aid kit is up to date and get your hands on a good solid machete. No, not to attack the other with, more to slash your way through what each of you will consider to be a rather dense, alien and challenging jungle. You, (2), are sensitive and caring and warm while you, (5), are the lone, dedicated seeker for the sake of the journey. “What is real?” is a question (5) asks all the time. You ready for that (2)? But, you never know till you give it a go. You’re almost two different species, so good luck.

We don’t mean to get morbid, but how often during WW II would have some Nazi ordered a peace-loving German soldier to shoot the hapless Jewish person standing in front of them, when the soldier in question has not only never hated any Jewish people at all, but is/has fallen in love with one of them? Honestly, what is it with human beings? Anyway, in some twisted way, could we imagine (5) as the dispassionate, single-minded Nazi, and the hapless soldier, who either has to do their job or be shot themselves, as (2)? Yes, we could. So, yes, good luck with this little romance!

The regulations stipulate that only so many people can stay over night in the homeless shelter due to the possible fire hazard, yet how does the person on reception, (2), knock back a young mum and her child when it’s cold outside? And of course, this has to occur right when the government inspector, (5), is making a routine visit. Both are only trying to do their job, and (5) would love more than anything to see this young family get a place tonight, but how would everyone feel if the nightmare happened due to overcrowding, and a fire did actually start? How can (5) possibly explain the potential horror of that outcome to these people? And you can’t argue with the maths. So what happens?….(2) is crying that they can’t say yes, the young mum is crying because she and her daughter have no where to stay, and (5) is even holding back the tears. Some problems are just too hard to deal with, eh?

(5) and (2) hop in the car and prepare to drive around the corner to visit a friend, and they’re only driving because it’s raining. (2) is behind the wheel because (5) has had a couple of wines, even though they’re only travelling 300 metres. (5) does their seat belt up and (2) doesn’t bother. 
“Are you going to do your seat belt up?” (5) asks.
“Nup, we’re just going around the corner.”
“Do you know that most car accidents happen close to home?”
“Nope.”
“Well they do, so do your seat belt up.”
“But I don’t feel like it. We’re not going far.”
And there ensues a mighty argument, which is only compounded by the weather. 
The End.

And once again we are cast into the future where, (5), the lovely and venerable house robot is trying to comfort it’s owner, (2), who has just broken up with their human partner and is sitting in the kitchen, sobbing. 
“What’s wrong, master?” (5) asks.
“Oh it’s nothing. I have a broken heart, that’s all.”
“Oh my god!” yells (5), who closes their eyes for one second before opening them again. “Don’t worry, I’ve just put a call out to an ambulance. Arrival time, seven minutes and forty seconds.”
“What? No, no, cancel that immediately! I’m not going to die, I just have a broken heart.”
“But master,” (5) says, concerned, “What do you mean?”

And there ensues a long, convoluted discussion, which is never going to have a satisfactory resolution.

No time for laziness here folks. No way. In a perfect world, the brilliant and dispassionate analytical skills of our NASA scientist, (5), are of tremendous help to the more flamboyant Launch Manager, (3). Likewise, the pizazz of (3)’s influence can be a tremendous addition to (5)’s philosophical/psychological quiver. In many ways (3) sees (5) as some kind of burrowing genius who just needs to be pointed in the right direction, which, in some cases, (5) might take quite personally. One proviso: If they begin competing with each other they’re screwed.

Never a dull moment with some couples, is there? There is no questioning (5)’s capacity to invent and to explore, and if ever they needed a good PR person then (3) would do a great job, although usually (3) has their own successful career to worry about. If they turn each other on then they’d have a grand old time in bed, but even outside the bedroom each provides the other with enough mental stimulation to keep everyone happy and enthused.

Like a fine and potentially expensive wine, these two definitely improve with age, mostly because both of them, in their own ways, are deep thinkers who can plan ahead and who realise moment-to-moment glory is largely a myth. And it helps too if they are not only recognised as being skilled and brilliant by each other, but also by those around them. We imagine the only real hiccup for (5) and (3), aside from potentially over-working, is if one person starts to let the team down by suddenly proving to be mediocre. But that’s not going to happen, right?

As an otter who has just constructed their best dam yet, (5) is constantly seeking to improve and to learn new ways of doing things. And while they secretly love the adulation from (3), who sat on the sidelines the whole while and offered small but pivotal pieces of advice whenever they saw fit, they won’t readily admit it. (3) on the other hand, kept reminding (5) that if they happened to come across a small crustacean during construction to grab it and toss it their direction for later, which (5) duly did. So, yes, they’re a fine if not slightly dysfunctional team, and we look forward to seeing how the dam holds up. Splendid.

Does (3) ever become somewhat disheartened by (5)’s apparent lack of compassion? Well, yes they do, but overall they’ve learnt not to take it personally. Likewise, (5) is accustom to (3)’s occasional emotional outbursts which tend to be funny rather than diabolical. In their eyes at least, anyway. What we have here is a highly functional pair of humans whose depths are far more intricate than what any of us might see on the surface. Maybe don’t ask (5) their opinion on how they are going - for things in their world either are or they aren't - but so far (3) is a pretty happy camper. And there’s our (current) answer.

At best, these two produce a long, in-depth team meeting and both of them have plenty to talk about. In the case of their respective brains functioning the same way, this would be great. However, we are confronted with two diametrically opposed personalities. (5), arguably the most clinical observer in the animal kingdom, very quickly becomes either bored or frustrated at how (4) constantly wants to talk about how they feel and what upsets them. Conversely, (4) is usually in a perpetual state of disbelief at how uncaring (5) seems to be. And don’t get (4) started on (5)’s apparent lack of intimacy and affection, heavens to mercy! We could be here all night.

(4) is the artist.
(5) is the scientist.
(4) is the campfire.
(5) is the bunsen burner.
(4) is the writer.
(5) is the editor, critic and publisher.
(4) lives largely inside themselves (to a large extent).
(5) almost never does (to a large extent). 
(4) needs deep connections.
(5) observes how or why deep connections are important. 
Are they good people?
Yes.
Are they a perfect match?
Mmmm…

(4)'s greatest wish for their partner is that they could unzip (5)’s head, pull out their brain, put it on for twenty minutes and see what they are really thinking or feeling. No, (5) isn’t the best at discussing these things, but only because on a list of priorities, pulling apart their deepest fears, hopes and emotions is somewhere near the bottom. Does this difference bode well for a long-lasting, close-knit relationship? We tend to think no, but, bless us all, humans are a weird and wonderful bunch and you just never know till you give it a try. Good luck!

Perhaps the largest hurdle for these two is for (5) not to become overwhelmed by (4)’s emotional intensity. In which case, does that mean they both have to act in a way which isn’t natural? Perhaps, then again maybe they just need to do that only a little, and get a bit of practice at it. In (5)’s case, maybe try not to mock a crazy idea as soon as (4) mentions it, or at least compliment them on one aspect of it before you pour cold water on it. And (4), if that happens, take the compliment, accept that (5) is trying to be considerate, but definitely don’t take any ensuing criticism personally. Remember (4), you and you alone are responsible for your happiness, and yep, that goes for everyone. Amen.

Can we look at that again in slow motion? Here we see (5) slowly turn back to the sink where they are in the middle of doing the dishes, having just whimsically suggested to (4), who is sitting at the kitchen table behind them, that they only watch television because they don’t have any meaningful hobbies in their life. Now, see the furrows of anger appear quite quickly on (4)’s forehead, as they instinctively snatch at their cup of water. (4) then hurls the cup at (5)’s back, and the vision of the water ejecting from the cup in slow motion on it’s way to impact is just brilliant. And then, here we see the shock of (5)’s body as water and cup crash into the back of them…..What a lovely, joyous morning.

Watching this pair is akin to the experience of sitting down to the fattest novel you’ve ever held. It starts off slow, with many of the early chapters giving only small, tantalising glimpses into what’s ahead. The characters to, they fro, they watch and they advise where some truth needs telling. 
Intrigued, you keep reading. It quickly becomes apparent that the pace of the plot is impeccable. Before you know it you’re fucking hooked. What a book. What a big, long, delicious journey. To read the trilogy might take years and so what? Why rush anything? 
In summary: These two observe their surroundings, they observe their partner and they act accordingly, with the notion of fun and truth at the forefront.
PS: if you’re not into books and don’t understand any of that, these two are probably not your friends, which means everyone is happy.

If encyclopaedias had a personality, and in all likelihood one day they will, in one form or another, then this is what they will resemble. Are these two a version of a perfect couple? We think yes, mostly because, to a large extent, and certainly more than any other coupling in the Kingdom, they have taken personal reactions and overt emotionality out of the equation. How did they do this? We don’t know, it’s just how they’re wired and it definitely works for them. But when life is good, these two think and talk and rationalise, and solve, and it’s beautiful.

Okay, and here we go with another AI image. You ready? Although you probably don’t need us to tell you what’s going on here because, finally, we have two splendid, human-looking robots who are not only geniuses in their own right, but their sense of humour is almost identical, their desire to learn is infinite, as are their respective memories, and they appear to enjoy the attention that their collective genius seems to attract. That’s right: robots with subtle egos. Who knows, pretty soon the rest of us might be able to design one to meet our own philosophical needs, but in the meantime these two don’t need us. They probably deserve a round of applause, though if they've never encountered applause before they may take a second to ascertain what you're doing.

From a human’s perspective two big killer whales, underwater next to each other, are a fantastic, awesome and quite humbling sight. That’s right, these two. And yes, they’re looking at you as well. No, they’re not going to eat you, though those couple of grunts you may have heard from them was a conversation they just had discussing this very issue. Mostly, if you haven't figured it out already, they are just supremely curious as to why such an ungainly looking animal is in the water at all. After a while, they start to feel sorry for us, and can you blame them? - our arms flailing about all over the shop, making silly noises and gesticulating for no apparent reason. Soon, they’ll get bored and swim off, impassive, perplexed but utterly serene, because there’s nothing we can offer them. And nor should we try. What a wonderful life.

And why did we choose this duo as the next team to live in the international space station? Easy. Because they strive for excellence in all that they do, they love a good experiment and debunking false theories, they do very well in a remote location which is bereft of distractions and idiots, they communicate incredibly well with each other and they rarely become so overawed that they forget what their task at hand is. Oh, and they’re not bad under pressure either, obviously. Right, so, wanna come watch the launch?

Yes, fascinating. These two function like a half-decent game of tennis. Intellectual discussions go back and forth for hours, even days and months, sometimes, and the reactions of the more emotional (6) might be crucial here. So long as they remain on each other’s side, they’ll be okay. Well, unless the more honest and grounded player, (5), gets sick and tired of the occasional tantrum thrown by the opponent, in which case they may very well just drop everything and walk off the court, mid-rant. Either way, they make for utterly fascinating viewing, and in the end both players usually come around.

If (5) is a heart surgeon then (6) is a GP who had a brief foray into applied psychology. As a result, this pair carry a wealth of knowledge, a vast amount of it over-lapping, and yes, (6)’s psych experiment means they’re better equipped to deal with the foibles of the average man or woman who happens to walking out of the supermarket, where as (5) hasn’t got the time or energy to listen to the petty woes of the scurrying lower middle classes. If they turn up on their operating table they'll will do the best they can, irrespective, but beyond that (5) will happily direct the patient to his more attentive partner. They should probably open some kind of practice together.

Once again we find ourselves at the dog shelter looking for a couple of pets to take home and make our own. Oh, here’s an interesting duo! (5), sitting calmly, is a large black poodle with a splendid pose, and they are watching us carefully, almost dispassionately. Next to (5) is fine-looking Border Collie, (6), who is sitting down for the moment, but is clearly a little perturbed by the situation. Either that or they’re just keen to get out of here and chase something. (5) looks down at (6) occasionally, barely registering a reaction, and what’s this, they come as a team? Well goodness, it looks like we have ourselves a family. The attendant opens the gate and (6) bounds out and then looks back at (5), who let’s out a big sigh, kinds of nod to their new human owners like they understand the English language, and away they all go. Marvellous.

These two are a fine team, although (5) is continually aghast that a partner of his, (6), though intelligent, conscientious and rather serene, usually, not only watches this sport called football on the television, but becomes as animated as they do. They don’t mind, really - after all, it doesn’t hurt anyone, (6) seems to enjoy themselves and if their ridiculous team wins it means there’s an elevated probability for some heated coitus later tonight - yet deep down it concerns (5) that (6) might be some kind of hidden idiot. Does (5) ponder these kinds of things about (6) often? Not really. Only on football nights.

QF787 en-route from San Francisco to Sydney has crashed on landing at Sydney airport. Miraculously, there were a dozen or so survivors, which is wonderful news, but sadly around two hundred passengers and crew have been killed. On hearing the news via a phone-call in their office, back at Boeing headquarters in the States, (5) lets out a deep breath. They put the phone down and look at their partner, (6). 
“Qantas has just had their first big accident,” (5) says calmly. “Go home and get your stuff. We’re flying out tonight.”
(6) nods, and though sadistically a little thrilled, for the sake of remaining cool in front of the boss they’ll keep a lid on it. (5) is the best air cash investigator Boeing has, and because these two go back a long way they’ve seen some pretty horrendous things together. This is going to be no different and they’ll do their job, but both of them are secretly glad they’re not going alone.

Like two opposing trench soldiers who know the only real differences between them are different shaped helmets and a different language, their true desires are to investigate and celebrate each other, which means these two can be a wonderful match. The calmer, more subtle of the duo, (5), provides a solid grounding for the highly energetic and more erratic (7), who in turn encourages the thinker to forget the laws of gravity and leap from the plane, to hop in with those piranha (so long as they don’t splash about), and to be bold, social and more brazen, in general. 
Likewise, (5) compels the amiable vagabond to steel themselves in moments of crisis and to ponder more deeply their words and actions. With these two, the universe suddenly doesn't feel very big at all.

Theoretically, these two should be fab. Brilliant, explorational (5) going out with the charismatic, free thinking social butterfly, (7), who doesn’t mind a bit of exploration themselves. What could go wrong? Actually, don’t answer that, plenty could go wrong: (5) might get tired of (7)’s child-like exuberance, (7) might tire of (5)’s perpetual lack of apparent enthusiasm, in fact, hold it, we could write a list which would take all day to read, but forget all that because, seemingly, they fit. (5) actually deeply admires some of (7)’s more lateral concepts - they certainly love their physical energy - and (7) loves the idea that (5) always keeps a foot on the ground, keeping them from getting too sidetracked. So, no pessimism here thanks folks. Let’s just watch the show.

While (5) generally hates a random dare, especially if it means they’ll be publicly humiliated, they hate being seen as being a stick in the mud way more. It’s an ego thing. So, when (7), who (5) just met upatairs at the party, suggested that it might be fun for both of them to run down stairs to the foyer, strip naked and run outside with the aim of jumping into the hotel’s fountain, what choice did (5) have? On so many levels they know it’s wrong, but how can one overlook such brazen joie de vivre? (7) is evidently not from Earth, and (5) is just about fed up with the rest of the Earthlings, so they’re in. 
The End…and the beginning.

Christ, never a dull moment is there, really? Certainly, not with these two in the room. Between (5)’s innate capacity to want to immediately get to the root cause of a problem, social dilemma, wive’s tale rumour, child’s behaviour, spouse’s behaviour, car’s behaviour, or you bloody-well name it, and (7)’s bouncing, nonchalant, lateral, suggestive, rude and untimely, if not occasionally brilliant suggestions, boredom is literally an impossibility here. Need we say any more? No. Shut up.

Well look at this will you? Just what we need, another bloody superhero, (7), and the brilliant behind-the-scenes-in-theory brains behind the operation, (5).  Is anyone else tired of superhero movies? We are, but we’re not tired of these two. In actual fact, we could probably make a movie just by filming them around home. No, they’re not saving the world, they’re just having an interesting, humorous, intelligent, tangental and rather splendid time amusing each other, testing each other, frustrating the shit out of each other, and living rather well. Is anyone out there doing the same? We suggest you try it. Over n out.

These two would have provided a wonderful spectacle and engendered a huge following had they been paired as a gladiatorial team inside the Roman colosseum two thousand years ago. The big, bolder and more professional warrior, (8), is perfectly complemented by their craftier, calmer and more careful ally, (5). The roar of the crowd and the sheer bloody conflict would inspire the former, while the highly technical, 3-dimensional nature of hand-to-hand battle is something the latter would get-off on. Having said that, no one has fun when they’re about to die, so perhaps these two are only meant to be together for a short time?

Can you imagine these two locked in a game of snooker? They’re both quite competitive, well, (8) is so competitive it’s ridiculous, and (5) is no slouch despite the cool exterior, but it would be a battle worth watching. True, part of (8)’s plan is to get the crowd involved and to rev them into a frenzy of support, where as (5), who has no visible opinion on this matter, is concentrating wholly on the balls on the table, calculating future events. Death or glory: this is what we have here folks, and can you just imagine the philosophical wrangling which would take place at home if they were a couple? It’d be worth paying money to watch. So, yes, on paper they’re good but in actuality we have no bloody idea. Talk to you later.

It’s not like (8) doesn’t ever help out - they’re actually an amazing, wonderful support - it’s just that they can’t do it constantly for months and weeks on end without come kind of pay back. Is this fair? We suppose it is, and we only mention it because of how dogmatic (8) is when things don’t go their way. And their capacity to have an elephant’s memory in so far as recalling what they’ve done for people, or a person, is frightening. But, all of that is rubbish when considering a partnership with (5). Why? Because (5) tells it like it is, pretty much straight away, and this is a trait (8) adores. Better than that, (5) is no fool and (8) knows this, and because they respect (5)’s opinion, despite also begrudging it sometimes, they will nearly always succumb to the truth. Got all that? Anyway, cut a long story short, these two are good. Amen.

Watching these two debate is like watching a mongoose have a go at a giant King Cobra. The mongoose, (5), is a mammal for a start, so it’s way more intelligent and it’s therefore better at making decisions and anticipating the immediate future, and it needs to be. (8), on the other hand, the big threatening presence is of course lethal, but all this posturing is only a front and (5) knows this very well. Even so, a lazy move on (5)’s behalf and it’s curtains, so they can’t let their guard down, nor do we expect them to. And deep down, you’d never know (8) is actually scared shitless right now, but we never told you that, orright? Anyway, as a couple, they’re like this all the time. They love it.

God, what a long-winded, drawn-out, melodramatic shemozzle this has turned into. The cops can’t arrest (8) just yet as there isn’t enough evidence. Detective Inspector (5) knows this, but they’re refusing to let (8) go until the hour is up, then legally they have no choice. You see, (8) really is guilty, (5) knows they’re guilty and (8) knows that (5) knows, but without any physical evidence, and without an admission, (5) is hamstrung and both of them know it. Right now (8) doesn’t mind being questioned, the cocky shit, but the whole thing is a facade. It’s like a dance, with these two, and it’ll go on until the big hand strikes twelve. 
Or until someone agrees they were once in love with so-and-so. Or until someone’s mother promises not to come next week. Or until someone admits that they were wrong. And round and round it goes. On and on and on. Thank god they’re pestering each other and not us. Goodnight.

“Shoosh, quiet please. This is a library and as you can see people are busy studying, working and preparing, as well as fitting-in with their surroundings as much as possible. What? Music? Shit no, no music. Well, only earplugs but even then make sure it’s not too loud. You’re permitted to make a coffee - just follow (9), one of our very attentive librarians over there. They’ll show you how, and they’re very friendly. Oh, and you want to know if anyone has fun in here? Well, of course they do. Look at that researcher, just here. That's (5) and they're here every day - reading up on the nature of the universe, we think. The only person they speak to is (9) and (9) assures us that, despite the frowns of concentration, (5) couldn’t be happier.” 
So, anyone up for a library visit?

Should these two be together? It’s a question their respective friends have been discussing amongst themselves behind their backs for months now. Lord knows, if they’re going to they’ll need their friends’ help in setting up some kind of contrived scenario, because (9) and (5) appear to spend too much time naval gazing, or staring into text books and self-help guides, respectively. It depends. So, presuming that does happen, and their peers help get them together, can we hope for a little greatness? Well, yes, you can lead a horse to water but you can’t make it drink, but in this case, oddly enough, and against the apparent odds, these two might do okay. Let’s just wait and see, shall we?…

Can (5) handle the emotional spectrum of (9)? 
Yep, we think so. 
Can (9) handle the aloof, almost analytical nature of (5)? 
Yes, probably, on the proviso (5) is, as is typically the case, interested in new ideas and is thoughtful and constructive with their responses. 
Are they good in bed? 
Dunno, check their sexual compatibility - not our business. 
Do they laugh?
Ummm, yes. Often, actually, although in a strange way neither of them, in hindsight, can actually pinpoint anything the other says as being particularly funny. Weird eh? 
Anyway, they’ll work it out.

Don't let the 60% put you off. These two are better suited to each other than they realise. Yes, there are philosophical and emotional differences, mostly in how they think and express themselves, and yes, while you may laugh that this is just about everything, there is actually quite a compassionate and close kind of vibe between them. Now, yes, we know (5), you detest that word almost as much as (9) appreciates it, but you know what we’re talking about here don’t you? There is a ‘vibe’, so pretend to ignore it as much as you like. Anyway, we’d suggest plonking these two in a big baking tray, dose them in a layer of time, cover them with nice cold sections of raw, silly humour, let them simmer under the heat of some gentle sexual curiosity, and let them stew in each others’ juices for a while. Amen.

If (5) is the bank robber who has spent years mapping-out their escape path, recording security rosters at the bank, monitoring the quietest times in the street, obtaining and preparing a getaway car etc, then (9) is the usually-capable accomplice who, on the morning of the robbery, suddenly decides they don’t want to hold a gun anymore and would be far happier if they both brandished some kind of stick instead. Truth be known, (9) has been feeling like this for a while but, due to (5)’s steadfast dedication to the plan, and their apparent glee at how it was all panning out - and lord knows (5) doesn’t express glee that often - they felt too guilty about bringing it up. 
“So why now?” (5) asks, more perplexed than angry. 
“I don’t know. Guns just don't feel right.”
At which point, (5) plunges their head into their hands because there goes two years of planning down the drain. And (9)’s chances for some make-up sex later are very slim.

If we imagine (1) as the decorated army lieutenant with high-minded ideals and a sense of organisation and discipline, then (6) is that soldier who, despite a fine record, was once discharged after being discovered smoking pot. Everyone was a winner probably, because no way was (6) ever going to shoot anyone, really. (They’re too humane for that kind of absurdity). 
But, out in the real world (1) appreciates (6)’s sense of humour, sometimes, as well as their sense of playfulness, so who can say how they’ll turn out? At their core they share many beliefs, it’s just the final expressions of behaviour which separates them. Perhaps all they need to do is make the decision to try? And they both joined up for a reason, yes?

Yes, we keep harping on about AI here, and where robots are heading, but if you don’t mind we’re going to use you two as another example. What do we mean? We mean that, as robots evolve they are going to arrive from the factory in stages of increasing intelligence, to the point where, maybe in 100 years or so, it might not actually be impossible to tell if someone is a robot or not. Have you seen Blade Runner and its sequel? Well, the early versions of hyper-intelligent robots will be a lot like (1): they’ll be brilliant, charming and funny, but they’ll probably be just a little too rigid in their thinking when compared to (6) - a much later version - who can toy with ideas better, adapt to change faster and be generally more sarcastic, as well as being way more likely to kill us all. Anyway, the point is, these two are very similar to one another, and us poor humans will just have to muddle along in our ignorance.

If you imagine (1) as the Park Ranger with an immaculate uniform and a penchant for keeping the rules, no matter what, then (6) is their loyal and rather more laid back colleague. On total fire band days (1) storms around the park, ensuring no rubbish is dropped on the ground and that no campfires are lit. (6), on the other hand, so long as (1) isn’t around, will happily chat with the campers and, hidden from view, toke on a quiet joint if offered but make no mistake, the welfare of the park and the campers is foremost in both their minds, and it’s a beautiful place that they both relish working in. As a team they do a wonderful job, and both compliment the other tremendously. Indeed, so long as these two are in attendance, there will be no fires, the campers will always leave happy and no rubbish will ever find its way into the local rivers. Amen.

Yep, so (1) is a stickler for protocol, they are confident and capable and generally covet an organised work station. (6) works in the same office, knows more people who work on different floors, chats to more people at the work Christmas party, and has less headaches about work after they arrive home. 
Do they both aspire to get the job done, and to do a fine job at that?
Absolutely.
Does (6) appreciate the methodology of (1) as being necessary to the group?
Yes.
Does (1) appreciate the same thing of (6)?
Yes.
Does a part of each of them respect and admire those parts in the other which are different?
Very much so. The End.

If (1) is the pilot not quite ready to skydive just yet, then (6) is the ex-pilot who gave flying away to sky dive, and who has now jumped out of planes 5,000 times. Both love being in the air, both have a very different take on how to navigate and move once they are doing their thing, and both feel just a tiny bit disappointed when their feet touch the ground. We’d imagine that, as a couple, they’ll be just fine.

These two would do well as a couple of Mormans because their devotion to duty and to one another is commendable. Solid commitment: this is what will work for these two. Pant-dropping, quick-sex-behind-the-barn isn’t really part of the equation here. Is that sad? Well, who can say. (6) will get occasionally pissed off with themselves and the world, and during these times (2) just needs to chill and not chase after them too much when (6) craves a little space. The thing is, is dependability the only criteria that’s important to each of you? If that’s the case then go get married, immediately, but there’s more excitement and magic in life to be had.

When they’re good, these two are great. So long as (6) has a little self-confidence and doesn’t over-think things, then (2) can be a wonderful, encouraging foil. But if (2) is the manager of the chemist and their chief pharmacist, (6), is in a sketchy mood, then (2) will feel like they have to manage not only the complaining customers, whose ailments seem to cover the whole spectrum of human woe, but both the shop and the dispensary and who has time for that? Mutual respect is important in life for all of us, but it’s definitely important here. Lose that and these two are screwed.

Were these two every incredibly turned on by one another, or, as we suspect may have been the case, was it a situation of gradual admiration and familiarity growing to a point where they seemingly had no choice but to take it to the next level? And there’s nothing wrong with that, is there?…

Maybe you believe in reincarnation and maybe you don’t, we’re not even sure we do, but for the sake of an example, let’s take (6) and (2). So, let’s presume, perhaps stupidly, that reincarnation exists, then one may not be totally incorrect by suggesting that (2) has been around a few more times than (6). Now, this is no criticism of (6), not by a long shot, it’s just that (2) is better at observing the bigger picture and (6) has a greater tendency to shut down if a situation isn’t to their liking. No, it not like this all the time, and they both have aspirations for a contented and loving home and family life, so, as ever, potential greatness is always just around the corner, but (2) is better at looking out, rather than looking in. Does that make sense?

Does (6) ever display the propensity for loving a bit of self-induced melodrama? And does (2) ever tire of this kind of self-absorption? The answer to both questions is a yes, but the variations on a theme take up way more space than we have room for here today. When (6) is good, they’re great, and when they’re down in the dumps they’re useless because they need constant attention and reinforcement. Fortunately (2) is good at this, and loves helping out, especially those they care about, but not if it carries on for too long. Does that sound familiar? No? Good, then I pronounce you husband and wife, or husband and husband, or wife and wife. Congratulations!

Here we have an event rarely seen in the wild, an Alsatian paired with an anxious but excitable Cocker Spaniel. At least they’re the same species, give or take, because they have plenty in common. The Alsatian, (3), is keen to get ahead, to complete the mission, to look good while it’s happening and to ultimately succeed by finding and devouring that hidden bone. Our Cocker Spaniel however, (6), is far more social and definitely more easily distracted. Make no mistake, (6) loves finding a hidden bone just as much as the next hound but their approach is vastly different, that’s all. Frustrations may appear from both sides but if they can manage to fluke getting a bone together then they might be okay.

Theoretically, these two are doing alright, but there are differences. For instance, if (3) and (6) are late to get to a wedding and (6) spies an injured animal by the side of the road, or perhaps an especially miserable-looking homeless person, then they will most likely insist (3) stop the car so they can both help somehow. True, this isn’t necessarily a bad thing for (3) - we all need to be compassionate for those who are suffering - and while (3) generally likes the fact (6) stands up for the less fortunate way more than they do, right now they need to be somewhere and this isn’t helping. But, (3) will do the right thing today, and they’ll be even later in arriving, however, if (6) pulls a similar stunt on the way home the shit will definitely hit the fan.

Yep, (3) is naturally more confident and self-assured than (6), and (6) can be a terrific support, although they are no slouch at working hard and achieving goals, either. Usually, (3) is more dynamic out there in the world, although (6) has a better grasp on some of life’s realities. Is the car due for a service? When can we get someone in to take care of the mould underneath these awnings? Can we organise someone to come and clip the dog’s claws? - these kinds of questions aren’t really on (3)’s radar, and usually they don’t mind stepping up once asked. It’s when (3) starts to repeatedly forget to do something that problems begin to fester and insecurities here seem to pile up quite quickly.
