Listen, if (6) ever starts taking (3)’s directives too personally, and it happens repeatedly, then the whole shebang will come crashing down in a heap in a matter of days. So (3), if you care about (6) just take half a second to analyse your words before they come out of your mouth. Yeah, yeah, we know - that’s tough, but it’s not beyond you and (6) is worth it, and they’re probably not quite as sensitive as we’re leading you to believe. So, a little gentleness here goes a long way. It’s your perceived arrogance, (3), that’s getting (6) worked up, so siddown and take a chill pill.

Do you ever lie back and marvel at the notion of why and how we just don’t all get along, having made the decision to be with someone? We don’t get it - don’t understand how so many people make a decision of their own volition, yet end up bickering and fighting and being disrespectful, and not acting with love as their purest intention. How did this come to be? We’re bloody sick of it, just now. Are you paying attention to (6)’s moods, (3)? Do you not understand that they’ll never be as driven as you? And do you (6) realise it’s your job to help (3) become a little more humane and compassionate? And it’s their job to bloody take heed of this. So, don’t freak out when (3) acts like a sanctimonious, arrogant pain in the arse. They’re trying to do their job and you are trying to do yours. Right. Good night.

Have you ever seen footage of two snakes engaged in coitus? You don’t know which snake is which, and here in a modern, human coupling we might be observing something very similar. Are (4) and (6) perfectly suited - the answer is a resounding YES! Talk about a match made in heaven, especially if each of them has already sorted out their emotional carry-on luggage. Then again, it probably doesn’t matter because, regardless, quite quickly each of them will feel like they are going out with their own private, brilliant psychiatrist. Perfect! The only issue, which is ours, is that if you are a friend of theirs then you might need to start looking around for some others.

Righto, who has the popcorn? These two are good. Do they both feel a little bit lost? Well not any more because finally each has met a like-minded soul, willing to bare all as a means to get to their own respective truths. Turns out both of them are loveable after all, although we could have told you that ages ago you pair of fools! In fact, that’s enough from us and we’ll leave it at that. Bravo! We’ll see you later, and if you decide to fill out all those forms and tick all those societal driven boxes, we’d love an invite to the wedding. Cheers.

Looking at (4) and (6) together is like looking at one of those pictures where someone is giving a giant eagle a hug, and where the eagle has their wings out and is hugging the human right back. Crazy, eh? You could say it’s corny but it’s also pretty remarkable. Maybe we’re just envious, but that looks like fun. Keep up the good work and we’ve nothing more to add.

These two are a fine pairing, and the only hiccup - well, one of the only hiccups - arises when or if (4) suggests to (6) that they try out the new nude beach. (6) isn’t necessarily as free-wheeling as (4), so this kind of suggestion might take them a little getting used to, but it’s a first world problem in our eyes. These kinds of suggestions is why (6) is with (4) in the first place. So, shall we just pop down the beach with our binoculars and see how they go?….Wicked!

Like a light in the dark, is how both (4) and (6) might describe their meeting each other. And how often does someone suggest something like that of their partner? That’s right, not very bloody often. True, they are a couple of hopeless romantics, (4) especially, and so they’re allowed the odd grandiose statement. Indeed, it’s quite refreshing in the modern era, where people toss around words like ‘awesome’ and ‘epic’ like throw-away confetti. Anyway, there is a real potential bond here that might very well last longer than just this summer. And bully for them if it does.

Yes, fascinating. These two function like a half-decent game of tennis. Intellectual discussions go back and forth for hours, even days and months, sometimes, and the reactions of the more emotional (6) might be crucial here. So long as they remain on each other’s side, they’ll be okay. Well, unless the more honest and grounded player, (5), gets sick and tired of the occasional tantrum thrown by the opponent, in which case they may very well just drop everything and walk off the court, mid-rant. Either way, they make for utterly fascinating viewing, and in the end both players usually come around.

If (5) is a heart surgeon then (6) is a GP who had a brief foray into applied psychology. As a result, this pair carry a wealth of knowledge, a vast amount of it over-lapping, and yes, (6)’s psych experiment means they’re better equipped to deal with the foibles of the average man or woman who happens to walking out of the supermarket, where as (5) hasn’t got the time or energy to listen to the petty woes of the scurrying lower middle classes. If they turn up on their operating table they'll will do the best they can, irrespective, but beyond that (5) will happily direct the patient to his more attentive partner. They should probably open some kind of practice together.

Once again we find ourselves at the dog shelter looking for a couple of pets to take home and make our own. Oh, here’s an interesting duo! (5), sitting calmly, is a large black poodle with a splendid pose, and they are watching us carefully, almost dispassionately. Next to (5) is fine-looking Border Collie, (6), who is sitting down for the moment, but is clearly a little perturbed by the situation. Either that or they’re just keen to get out of here and chase something. (5) looks down at (6) occasionally, barely registering a reaction, and what’s this, they come as a team? Well goodness, it looks like we have ourselves a family. The attendant opens the gate and (6) bounds out and then looks back at (5), who let’s out a big sigh, kinds of nod to their new human owners like they understand the English language, and away they all go. Marvellous.

These two are a fine team, although (5) is continually aghast that a partner of his, (6), though intelligent, conscientious and rather serene, usually, not only watches this sport called football on the television, but becomes as animated as they do. They don’t mind, really - after all, it doesn’t hurt anyone, (6) seems to enjoy themselves and if their ridiculous team wins it means there’s an elevated probability for some heated coitus later tonight - yet deep down it concerns (5) that (6) might be some kind of hidden idiot. Does (5) ponder these kinds of things about (6) often? Not really. Only on football nights.

QF787 en-route from San Francisco to Sydney has crashed on landing at Sydney airport. Miraculously, there were a dozen or so survivors, which is wonderful news, but sadly around two hundred passengers and crew have been killed. On hearing the news via a phone-call in their office, back at Boeing headquarters in the States, (5) lets out a deep breath. They put the phone down and look at their partner, (6). 
“Qantas has just had their first big accident,” (5) says calmly. “Go home and get your stuff. We’re flying out tonight.”
(6) nods, and though sadistically a little thrilled, for the sake of remaining cool in front of the boss they’ll keep a lid on it. (5) is the best air cash investigator Boeing has, and because these two go back a long way they’ve seen some pretty horrendous things together. This is going to be no different and they’ll do their job, but both of them are secretly glad they’re not going alone.

Such a sensitive couple, aren’t they? They almost make you want to tiptoe around the house. Why are they so thin-skinned? Anyone? Anyway, so long as they know no naked photos of anyone are going end up on the internet (or any great secrets divulged) they’ll get on well, they’ll laugh a lot, they’ll orgasm simultaneously once in a while (if they’re lucky) and they’ll enjoy dinners both alone and in company. The sheer fact is that their intrinsic similarities form the glue which holds them together. Hopefully this comes from a good place, where mutual admiration and a kindred sense of fun are the dominating forces, not one where one party feels like they need constant rescuing.

Well, in a glass-is-half-full, scenario, here we have two fun, sensitive souls who are each standing in front of a mirror, looking at themselves. Yes, these two are very similar in what they need and desire from the world, and though these are two quite different things, the respective members of this duo are presented with a safe canvas upon which to lay out all that they are, and to bare their deepest thoughts and fears knowing they won’t be torn apart by the other. Trust: this what’s on today’s menu kiddies, and lots of it. If we have it, we may all end up with free tickets to the opera. Splendid.

Kanye West and Eminem? ...Eh? Nah, K.D Lang and Ed Sheeran more like it, that’s the mood we have with these two, ladies and gentlemen. Subtlety, gentleness, serenity - definitely no knickers tossed at the stage tonight thanks. Well, you know, within reason of course. One night stands aren’t really the biscuits these two have ever really enjoyed chewing on - though they’ve had their moments up to now, of course - but like two timid horses who needed to be approached very slowly, these two finally seem to have their shit together. What they do now is none of our business, but we think it’s looking pretty good.

Biologists have been trying to capture footage of them for years, and finally they have it. Two marsupial mice, way out in the middle of the desert, thought to be extinct, and now via new motion sensors and infrared cameras, we see the dance at last. And it’s complex. Look at them, moving around each other shyly, darting away and darting back, baring their teeth and buttocks more and more in a strange dance known only to them, moving more freely every time, until they realise this is the one. Oh my lord! What an ornate, dazzling display, and who would have thought it would come from these two? We understand now why we never glimpse them together in daylight. Phew, righto, let’s head home and take them off the endangered species list.

Once more we find ourselves back in the ocean, and late in the day we are down near the bottom of a reef, under a ledge, and there, do you see them? Two small sea horses. If you look closely you’ll see the male carrying all the eggs - pretty cool huh? Mum doesn’t mind. She trusts him. In fact, without that these two are nothing. So, just take it easy and don’t make any sudden moves. They’re nice, eh? They look happy - like they haven’t got a care in the world because they have each other, and no one and nothing has any idea they’re down here. Just how they like it. The End.

If we imagine (7) as the renegade bikie, with only a red bandanna protecting their cranium, and (6) as the highway motorcycle patrol cop with a glistening black helmet they take great pleasure in keeping very shiny, then we are close to seeing these two at play. Both are deeply committed to the roar of their bikes and the open road, it’s just that the parameters under which they each use the space are vastly different. One accidentally breaks the rules, or at least, gives this impression, while the other gets embarrassed about not having their uniform neatly pressed. So, how can these two work? Oddly enough, it’s not necessarily the fiasco one might imagine. They’re both nude in the shower, they both love the sound of their engines and while (6) can help (7) with the intricacies of how not to get arrested, (7) gets (6) excited about the idea of riding across Europe and attending a nudist camp, who otherwise wouldn’t have thought of it. They’ll work it out.

If (7) is the eccentric composer with Asperger’s, then (6) is the their wonderful assistant whose job it is to sit at the piano while (7) sings and groans and waves their hands in the air as a means to convey the sounds of a new symphony their are endeavouring to dictate. Diligent and capable (6) is watching and listening intensely, reciting back on the piano what they think (7) is musically preaching and they’re a fine team, with a couple of noted concertos under their belts already. Do they occasionally frustrate the shit out of each other? You betcha, but we think that’s their job, so, let’s wish them well, leave them to their trivial but highly entertaining bickering and we’ll see you all in London for the premiere. Tally ho!

Poor, peaceful, gentle, loyal (6). How they wound up being coerced to manage the finances of the cities most notorious gangster, (7), they’ll never know. Sadly, the rumours are true though, because being inducted into the mob is like getting addicted to surfing: once you're in you’re in, and you’re in it for life whether you like it or not. (6) wouldn't mind so much if only (7) did what they asked them to do because (7) deplores all admin, obviously, and so despite (6) knowing every loophole there is, without (7)’s compliance with even the most basic of instructions - I mean, how difficult is it to sign one bloody form? - then the whole organisation is in peril. And who do you think is going to cop the blame for that one? Ironically, (6) genuinely likes (7). Did from the first meeting, and they’ve always gotten on well, so we'll just keep watching the show, eh?

These two could do very well, so long as (6) doesn’t tire of apparently taking the back seat inside the various scenarios of regular melodrama and chaos which (7) either attracts, creates or actually drags them in to. On the other hand, (7) might get occasionally fed up with (6) saying no to everything all the time, accusing them of being a constant naysayer. Nine times out of ten, (6) only reacts this way because they know neither of them have the time, money or the resources to implement such ridiculous plans, and they nearly always are. If (6) has said it once they’ve said it a thousand times: going out with (7) is like going out with an effing teenager. On the flip side, naturally, when they’re on the same page or even close, there is a huge well of fun to be tapped into here, on both sides, and surely that’s worth the ride for both of them?

Hmmm, maybe 70% was a bit optimistic for these two, we’re not sure. On a bad day (7) is truly irresponsible and reckless, looking only at the future and the big picture, with no grounding in reality whatsoever and even less left to care about what their behaviour means for anyone else. (6), on a similarly cloudy day, is pessimistic, overcareful, mistrustful and non-compliant, but at least they have some idea about the consequences of their actions. But, let’s not be miserable for a second. When they’re in sync, and looking at each other, and being aware of the full scope of both of their better qualities, then, by god, (6) and (7) can just about nut out any problem, out perform the best of them and derive more than enough laughter and fun from what they co-create to last a life time. So, who feels like their cup is now on the way to being overflowing, no matter how little juice remains?

Is that wedding bells I hear? The staunch ball-breaker, (8), has their perfect foil in (6) and it seems to be a recurring theme with these in-your-face types. What do you do?
They’re like a couple of lionesses who share the same goal of keeping the pride together. Naturally, one is more boisterous than the other because rarely in nature can two A-type leaders hold the same stage. But, it works. At least, it works most of the time. Don’t let the roars of occasional frustration fool you, nor the play-wrestles which you would swear were about to result in someone having their throat torn out, it’s just how they are and they love it.

Wow, will you look at this castle? Look at the sheer size of it! Check out those parapets! From up there you’d see the enemy coming before the enemy even knew they were going to be your enemy. Jeepers! Well, no one and no army is getting in here folks, so if you don’t have an invite and the draw bridge is up you might as well turn around and head back to where you’re from. How many people built this thing anyway? Anyone know?….Yep. Two people built it, (6) and (8). And if you haven’t seen them don’t be worried, they’re pretty careful about who they let in to their fortress of trust, mutual admiration, strength and overall brilliance although they do secretly love people coming to take photos of it. Anyway, if you do get in, somehow, can you give us a call? We’d like to interview them.

Is (8) ostensibly the captain of the ship? 
Most definitely, yes, and not even ostensibly. 
Does (6) enjoy the captain’s methods?
Yes. Indeed, as First Mate, they see to (8)’s every command with promptness and commitment to the cause. Lashings happen but they are rare. 
Does (6) ever get to take over the running of the ship?
Yes, but only when they’re in port, and as yet (8) has never been so ill at sea as to need to hand ultimate leadership over to anyone.
Does (8) trust (6)’s capacity to do a good job in such a situation?
….Yes.
Has the ship been successful in battle, so far?
They have never lost a battle, and more over, they have captured quite a healthy booty from several foreign raiders, who suddenly found themselves in the position of having bitten off way more than they could chew. (8) was apparently very impressed with (6)’s levels of initiative and courage. 
Are they due back in port any time soon?
We’re not sure. Last we heard moral was good. Crew was healthy and the captain and first mate were in fine fettle.

Yes that’s them, outside the restaurant screaming at one another in full view of the diners inside, and we suspect (8) instigated the whole thing. You see, (8) accused (6) of being a hypocrite because (6) just selected a living crayfish from the tank they’d like killed and cooked for their dinner, and according to (8), (6) raves on about the mistreatment and debasement of animals by human beings quite a bit. Anyway, what started as a gently gybe got completely out of hand, and this is what they do. Well, from time to time anyway. It’s great viewing, eh? Any second now (6) will get down on their knees and feign allegiance to their illustrious moral leader, and not long after that they’ll get in the car and drive home and shag their brains out. Categorically nothing to worry about. They’re fine.

Question: does (8) enjoy being lauded as some kind of living legend?
Mmmm….yes.
Does (6)?
Not so much.
Is (6) as capable of genius and success as (8)?
Yes.
Does (6) really believe that?
Mmmm….maybe yes maybe no, but it’s tough for them in the presence of you-know-who.
Does (6) handle confrontation as well as (8)?
No. No one does. 
Is (6) a loyal and wonderful supporter of (8)?
We think so, yes.
Can we same the same of (8)?
Believe it or not, but actually, yes. (8) is a tremendous supporter of (6) and probably their biggest fan.
The End.

Common as muck, this type of couple. Why is that? Well, (6) wants to obey the laws of the land and ensure they never change their job or their eating habits while (9) is dead-keen on paying off their mortgage and attaining ‘independence’. Big Brother and the tax department loves these two, and you may have noticed that the television networks are trying to brainwash the population into thinking and behaving the same way. Anyway, when you meet them we can only suggest that you refrain from making any sudden movements or making loud, unexpected noises. They get easily startled and once you scare them off there’s no way they’ll come back in a hurry. Life is a surprising, chaotic beast to deal with, usually, and we wonder if this lack of capacity to deal with quick surprises has anything to do with a huge divorce rate? Be that as it may, we wish them all the best.

And here we have our proud and healthy horse, (6), with a tremendously shiny coat and well-polished hooves. Excellent. And here we have (9), our friendly, kind of dopey and extremely chilled-out donkey who doesn’t really mind too much about anything really, and whose sole job is to just kind of hang around in the paddock and keep (6) company, and to make them feel a little bit special. (6) enjoys being viewed as a lovely, potentially powerful and responsible individual, where as (9) loves chaff and the more carrots they receive in the morning the better. Are they a happy couple? Aaah, well, ignorance is bliss, true, but we’d say that usually, they’re doing okay. How’s that?

Do these two need a sea change? Should they just sell-up the whole thing and get a tiny little shack down the coast? Well, (6) likes the idea on paper and it was (9)’s in the first place, but the wheels of change take a long time to turn in some households and this one is no exception. But, they’ll talk about it for a long while until after a year or two or three of (9) being genuinely excited that they might finally get to live near the ocean, it seems (6) has finally bared their true feelings on the issue: Mental stimulation might be a tough for (6) with nothing to do other than buy organic veggies from beach-side markets and they never really like the idea of fishing in the first place. So, what to do? We know, come back in a year and find out. Amen.

If there is a wee problem beginning to develop with the car, (9) is more likely to take the attitude of ignoring it and hoping it just gets better, where as (6) will either try and determine exactly what the issue is, or find someone who will. One way or the other the problem is going to be fixed, and perhaps (9)’s role is to keep (6) motivated and happy while they go about their business? (9) is definitely not likely to fuss and worry, thereby getting in (6)’s face. Actually, (6) would probably appreciate a bit more of that from (9), but then they wouldn’t be (9). Anyway, in that regard they’re not a bad couple…..and maybe 50% slightly underestimates them?

Ever seen The Big Lebowski? (9), ‘The Dude’, and (6), ‘Walter’, love playing ten pin bowls but the means with which they each receive joy from the enterprise are quite different. Are they a good couple? Well, yes and no, and like everything in life there are good bits and bad. (9) is not so much lazy as they are ambivalent, and (6), while entertaining and obviously intelligent, is a little wound-up. It’s certainly entertaining to watch. Let us know how they get on.

Like a drug-addicted, effervescent clown, (7), having a relationship with well-paid tax attorney, (1), there is a slim chance that they might actually complement one another brilliantly, so there must be some hope, right? The fun/freedom-seeking (7) may actually encourage (1) to chill-out and take things less seriously. Likewise, (1) might aid (7) to stay focussed and to finish what they begin, but everyone doubts it, even them. Whatever happens it’ll be fun to watch and the best part is that these two will at least be well-equipped to see the humour in their own demise. Hell, it might even be the reason the universe plonked them together in the first place.

You don’t often witness a police officer falling in love with the bank robber they happened to catch, do you? Maybe that’s a good thing. Our loveable bank robber, (7), who can barely sit still for more than 10 minutes, didn’t really mind being arrested by (1). Part of them actually appreciates the work ethic and dedication (1) must have applied in order to find them in the first place. (7) simply can’t imagine being that diligent over such a long time. (1), on the other hand, might secretly wish they could go to work for one day and have the next year off, but to break the law? They’ll probably never get their head around that one. So, a fun little tryst, only, is what might be on offer here, unless (1) decides to try and help (7) break out of jail. I guess we’ll all wait for the telemovie to tell us what happened…

Seen Topgun? The original? Well, that man in the control tower who repeatedly denied Maverick permission to fly a low pass over the airfield is (1) - and don’t for a second think they don’t do a bloody fine job, without which plenty of people would die - and Maverick is (7). Anyway, that’s the short version. Are they suited romantically? ….What do YOU reckon?

And here we have (1), our King or Queen, born into the role and therefore with little thought or chance of opting out, who is obliged to maintain a certain regimented level of organisation across the realm - after all, why would a peasant farmer pay taxes to a leader who constantly cracks jokes, mucks around and seemingly has no care in the world? On the other hand, that is (7)'s job as court jester: to maintain levity and a sense of fun at all times, and to amuse and diffuse those in court who might otherwise bore us all to death. So (7) has a role to play, make no mistake, and which is usually appreciated by (1). Don’t think they don’t, it’s just that (7) is never going to be knighted, for that would mean that (1) deeply, truly and publicly adored the silly rascal. And that, ladies and gentlemen, would be what we call a scandal.

In cartoon terms, these two are like the Roadrunner and the Coyote. Do you think you can guess who is who? We’re not going to tell you, it’s so obvious. Suffice to say, being the aggressor requires planning, it requires patience and it requires intelligence, well, theoretical intelligence anyway. And what does our goofy Roadrunner have to do? Sweet bugger all. Their only aim in life is to run like the wind, smile like a bloody idiot, and frustrate those in their midst who would aim to diminish the amount of fun they are currently having. Does Coyote ever stop and admire Roadrunner’s capacity to live in this moment?….Not often. And does the Roadrunner ever take a second to appreciate the amount of preparation Coyote puts in, in order to try and catch him? …Shit no. So no, we don’t expect too much from this coupling.

(2) is the kind of romantic who insists albatrosses mate for life, while (7) knows that, deep down, albatrosses, male and female, are wonderful tarts and occasionally excellent actors, and these disparate opinions sum these two up. (7)’s joie de vivre is adored by (2), who find them terribly exciting. Likewise (7) loves how (2) can calm them down and keep their eyes pointed at the job at hand, but often the greater level of intimacy required by (2) is too constrictive for our bouncing (7). Having said that, they generate an incredible amount of warmth for those around them and perhaps this is their gift for the world? Maybe they should consider opening an orphanage somewhere?

Yep, these two can be fantastic together. True, (7) is hardly ever home because there always seems to be some function which needs either attending or organising, and when they are home (2) is often on the phone to a friend in crisis - and lord knows (2) is a wonderful, caring shoulder to cry on - but they manage to find a way. And when they are home together and (2) isn’t on the phone, so long as they are attentive to each other then there is no reason why these two won’t go a long way. Amen.

This couple is often the life of the party. (7) does the entertaining, whether they mean to or not, and invariably (2) winds up helping at least one person who has a problem that they need to get off their chest, which they enjoy. Usually, (2) is very aware that (7) needs their space and likewise, (7) knows that (2) needs more intimacy that they are probably accustom to providing, but the generous nature of both of them somehow manages to figure out a solution which makes everyone happy most of the time. And that’s the secret for all us, right?

The only date on the calendar that presents a problem for these two is that of their wedding anniversary. Why? Because (7) barely remembers it, in lieu of the fact they don’t seem to remember much about anything, and (2) will always have a deeper need for their love and affection to be actively recognised. Question is, is this something that will strike a unrecoverable wedge between them? The answer, we think, is a resounding no, but it’s probably a salient little lesson for (7). Just remember (7), yes, you ‘re the centre of the show, but deep down you know this is a selfish load of shit, don’t you? Anyway, you two will be alright. And (2), our advice, if it really bothers you, just get (7) hammered one night and lead them to a tattoo parlour so they can get the date tattooed on their arm, or something.

And here we find our charismatic and skilled coffee maker, (7), in a fine mood. The coffee is coming out of the machine nicely, the milk is frothing easily, but not too much, and as ever, the patrons are regularly complimenting them on their fine brews. But why hasn’t the boss, (2), mentioned anything about how good their coffee is yet? (7) is beginning to worry. (2) on the other hand is in charge of this town's busiest cafe, and they have more than one task to attend to at any given time. Sure, their morning coffee was lovely, but with all they have to do, how or even should (7) constantly need to be told how wonderful they are? They’ll figure it out, we imagine, but mostly, and like the patrons sitting around looking smug and content, we just enjoy the energy these two bring to the establishment. And we’ll be back tomorrow watch them do it all again.

Watching (3) and (7) is exhausting enough, and we certainly can’t imagine what it’s like actually being in the relationship. Like watching the formation of a new star or some such phenomena, the amount of noise, light and heat generated by these two means that we, as observers, probably need to bring sedatives, a good chair, sunglasses and definitely some water to cool us down. These two never sit still and their arguments can be highly entertaining, especially for each other. Together they are kids at heart and if, heaven forbid, someone gets seriously hurt or offended then the ending will be swift and they’ll hopefully forget about each other, soon enough.

These two are a riot. And most likely famous. How they stay together is largely beyond us because they attract so much energy and brilliance that surely someone’s head is likely to just pop off one night, mostly out of pure excitement. We’re not kidding. As usual, (3) often has to do the apologising or explaining after (7) has accidentally destroyed something expensive in someone’s house, but what do you do? According to (7), if nothing is destroyed during a party then it’s not a  party. The only issue, if they have one, is that (3) will always work harder and dedicate more time to their career. (7), as you might expect, goes out of their way to avoid the use of such terms altogether. Anyway, they’ll be fine.

(3) has tried explaining to (7) that they can’t just blurt out what they’re thinking any time they feel like it. 
“Did I offend someone?” (7) will ask, genuinely surprised.
“(7), did you not see the look on his face when you reminded his partner that you slept with them, back in Chicago?”
“Oh shit, did I say that?”
(3) shakes their head. “Listen, I don’t care who you slept with, you know that, but can you just try and take a second next time. I was embarrassed for him.”
(7) smiles and says, “Well, yeah, okay…but you have to admit it was pretty funny, eh? If I really said that, I mean.”
“It was bloody hilarious (7), but that’s not the point!”

And then they probably went and had some ‘pretend make up sex’ just for the hell of it.

These two can achieve just about anything. At their best they could make themselves famous, or at least one of them anyway, if they’re hunting that type of thing. They attract people and events and are, generally speaking, larger than life. At their worst, which doesn’t seem to happen too frequently, they’ve been known to set entire apartment blocks on fire, crimes of passion have happened, cars have been wrecked and insurance companies have wanted them killed. But as we say, this is in no way the norm. (3) and (7) have the capacity to be utterly brilliant, and we’ll be watching them closely.

It's lucky they have a budget to work with because in each other’s company neither of them is any good at saying the word NO. In fact, that about sums these two up. Last we heard they were sailing a yacht through Greece, but at (7)’s insistence, so the rumour goes, (3) agreed to see if they could sail all the way to New York. Anyone know if they’ve arrived yet? Hold on, hold on, is this story bullshit or is it legit? Oh wait! No way! (3) has just sent us a text……

Oh my god….you’re not going to believe what’s happened! 

(Moral to the story: (3) and (7) are a grand, life changing duo. The end.)

Unless these two are heavily into BDSM, or a have a fetish for Chinese riverboats, or perhaps they developed a penchant training and flying pigeons, they are screwed. They’re just too different. (7) craves the wind through their hair and miles and miles of paddocks to run across, naked, preferably,  while (4) dotes on the idea of rubbing each others’ fingernails in the morning with that special someone, whispering little secrets. 
Yes, we’re talking chalk and cheese. We’re talking flashlights and watermelons. We’re talking suspenders on a cactus plant. 
Forget the whole thing.

(7) staggers in the door, smelling of booze and with a twisted smile on their face, having hardly slept for two days, to discover (4) standing next to an intimate looking table-for-two in the dining room, which they prepared two nights ago.
“…Uh oh,” (7) says, after they get their bearings.
“Yep. Uh oh is right,” replies (4).

And there endeth the lesson.

Like a determined, loving and usually-forgiving Tibetan monk, (4), holding on to the tail of a Bengal tiger, (7), who is desperate to get some food or fun into their gob, there is a reasonable probability that if the tiger isn’t sated soon, they’ll just turn around and eat the monk. Not out of malice, mind you. (7) is just hungry, and perhaps a little bored, and (4) just happens to be the nearest option.

“Hey, do you want to go see that band, tonight?” asks (7), sticking their head around the corner into the bathroom.
“Um, well I thought we could stay in,” replies (4). “There’s a couple of things I want to talk to you about. Plus we haven’t eaten at home for ages.”
(7) looks surprised. “Oh, okay. We’ve got five minutes now. What’s up?”
“Well, no, can’t we have a nice dinner together? It might take a while.”
“Alright,” (7) sighs. “I’ll be back by six. If we’re eating early it means we’ll have time for the band. I’ll just go downtown and get the tickets. See you soon.”
Before (4) can complain (7) has vanished out the door, which gives them plenty of time to wonder how long they can do this for.

If (4) is the rather gentle and gifted nature photographer then (7) is a Viking chieftain, and it would seem one of them has been transported either forward or back in time to a place in which they may not survive very long. Certainly, we don’t expect them to cope too well together, although (7) would make a tremendous subject for (4), and god knows that if (7) is going to survive in the modern world they’ll need some advice on how to behave. It might be a short-run thing but it might be fun to watch, eh?

Like two opposing trench soldiers who know the only real differences between them are different shaped helmets and a different language, their true desires are to investigate and celebrate each other, which means these two can be a wonderful match. The calmer, more subtle of the duo, (5), provides a solid grounding for the highly energetic and more erratic (7), who in turn encourages the thinker to forget the laws of gravity and leap from the plane, to hop in with those piranha (so long as they don’t splash about), and to be bold, social and more brazen, in general. 
Likewise, (5) compels the amiable vagabond to steel themselves in moments of crisis and to ponder more deeply their words and actions. With these two, the universe suddenly doesn't feel very big at all.

Theoretically, these two should be fab. Brilliant, explorational (5) going out with the charismatic, free thinking social butterfly, (7), who doesn’t mind a bit of exploration themselves. What could go wrong? Actually, don’t answer that, plenty could go wrong: (5) might get tired of (7)’s child-like exuberance, (7) might tire of (5)’s perpetual lack of apparent enthusiasm, in fact, hold it, we could write a list which would take all day to read, but forget all that because, seemingly, they fit. (5) actually deeply admires some of (7)’s more lateral concepts - they certainly love their physical energy - and (7) loves the idea that (5) always keeps a foot on the ground, keeping them from getting too sidetracked. So, no pessimism here thanks folks. Let’s just watch the show.

While (5) generally hates a random dare, especially if it means they’ll be publicly humiliated, they hate being seen as being a stick in the mud way more. It’s an ego thing. So, when (7), who (5) just met upatairs at the party, suggested that it might be fun for both of them to run down stairs to the foyer, strip naked and run outside with the aim of jumping into the hotel’s fountain, what choice did (5) have? On so many levels they know it’s wrong, but how can one overlook such brazen joie de vivre? (7) is evidently not from Earth, and (5) is just about fed up with the rest of the Earthlings, so they’re in. 
The End…and the beginning.

Christ, never a dull moment is there, really? Certainly, not with these two in the room. Between (5)’s innate capacity to want to immediately get to the root cause of a problem, social dilemma, wive’s tale rumour, child’s behaviour, spouse’s behaviour, car’s behaviour, or you bloody-well name it, and (7)’s bouncing, nonchalant, lateral, suggestive, rude and untimely, if not occasionally brilliant suggestions, boredom is literally an impossibility here. Need we say any more? No. Shut up.

Well look at this will you? Just what we need, another bloody superhero, (7), and the brilliant behind-the-scenes-in-theory brains behind the operation, (5).  Is anyone else tired of superhero movies? We are, but we’re not tired of these two. In actual fact, we could probably make a movie just by filming them around home. No, they’re not saving the world, they’re just having an interesting, humorous, intelligent, tangental and rather splendid time amusing each other, testing each other, frustrating the shit out of each other, and living rather well. Is anyone out there doing the same? We suggest you try it. Over n out.

If we imagine (7) as the renegade bikie, with only a red bandanna protecting their cranium, and (6) as the highway motorcycle patrol cop with a glistening black helmet they take great pleasure in keeping very shiny, then we are close to seeing these two at play. Both are deeply committed to the roar of their bikes and the open road, it’s just that the parameters under which they each use the space are vastly different. One accidentally breaks the rules, or at least, gives this impression, while the other gets embarrassed about not having their uniform neatly pressed. So, how can these two work? Oddly enough, it’s not necessarily the fiasco one might imagine. They’re both nude in the shower, they both love the sound of their engines and while (6) can help (7) with the intricacies of how not to get arrested, (7) gets (6) excited about the idea of riding across Europe and attending a nudist camp, who otherwise wouldn’t have thought of it. They’ll work it out.

If (7) is the eccentric composer with Asperger’s, then (6) is the their wonderful assistant whose job it is to sit at the piano while (7) sings and groans and waves their hands in the air as a means to convey the sounds of a new symphony their are endeavouring to dictate. Diligent and capable (6) is watching and listening intensely, reciting back on the piano what they think (7) is musically preaching and they’re a fine team, with a couple of noted concertos under their belts already. Do they occasionally frustrate the shit out of each other? You betcha, but we think that’s their job, so, let’s wish them well, leave them to their trivial but highly entertaining bickering and we’ll see you all in London for the premiere. Tally ho!

Poor, peaceful, gentle, loyal (6). How they wound up being coerced to manage the finances of the cities most notorious gangster, (7), they’ll never know. Sadly, the rumours are true though, because being inducted into the mob is like getting addicted to surfing: once you're in you’re in, and you’re in it for life whether you like it or not. (6) wouldn't mind so much if only (7) did what they asked them to do because (7) deplores all admin, obviously, and so despite (6) knowing every loophole there is, without (7)’s compliance with even the most basic of instructions - I mean, how difficult is it to sign one bloody form? - then the whole organisation is in peril. And who do you think is going to cop the blame for that one? Ironically, (6) genuinely likes (7). Did from the first meeting, and they’ve always gotten on well, so we'll just keep watching the show, eh?

These two could do very well, so long as (6) doesn’t tire of apparently taking the back seat inside the various scenarios of regular melodrama and chaos which (7) either attracts, creates or actually drags them in to. On the other hand, (7) might get occasionally fed up with (6) saying no to everything all the time, accusing them of being a constant naysayer. Nine times out of ten, (6) only reacts this way because they know neither of them have the time, money or the resources to implement such ridiculous plans, and they nearly always are. If (6) has said it once they’ve said it a thousand times: going out with (7) is like going out with an effing teenager. On the flip side, naturally, when they’re on the same page or even close, there is a huge well of fun to be tapped into here, on both sides, and surely that’s worth the ride for both of them?

Hmmm, maybe 70% was a bit optimistic for these two, we’re not sure. On a bad day (7) is truly irresponsible and reckless, looking only at the future and the big picture, with no grounding in reality whatsoever and even less left to care about what their behaviour means for anyone else. (6), on a similarly cloudy day, is pessimistic, overcareful, mistrustful and non-compliant, but at least they have some idea about the consequences of their actions. But, let’s not be miserable for a second. When they’re in sync, and looking at each other, and being aware of the full scope of both of their better qualities, then, by god, (6) and (7) can just about nut out any problem, out perform the best of them and derive more than enough laughter and fun from what they co-create to last a life time. So, who feels like their cup is now on the way to being overflowing, no matter how little juice remains?

Theoretically this is a brilliant coupling but one large question looms: how many bouncing, easily-bored, chicken-brained thrill-seekers can one duo handle?
It’d be like living in a house full of Sagittarians. No one would remember to pay the electricity bill, taps in the upstairs baths would be forgotten to be turned off because of the music volume, and don’t get us started on the car’s insurance policy, given the accident which only happened this morning. For god’s sake, someone has to have their feet on the ground, don’t they? Life can’t be a party all the time, can it? At least, this is what some of their friends endeavour to tell these two, but not much of it is getting in. Make no mistake, they hold the loudest, longest gatherings in the city, but as a long-term, functioning relationship?

Most middle class couples these days seem to have two cars. One is for the family - to fit the kids and the dogs in - and the other is often a slightly smaller, runaround vehicle used primarily to fetch the bread and milk which everyone forgot to get. And there shall be no such level-headed thinking under this roof, thank you very much. Not only do we have two, two-seated sports cars parked out front, but they’ve taken out another mortgage just to pay for them. Now, is this going to work in the long run? Sad thing is, so long as there is some kind of immediate fun to be had, neither of them really care. But fear not, as soon as we see them tying one of the kids to the bonnet for a trip to the beach - given they obviously won’t all fit in two cars - we’ll call the cops.

Like watching a tiny fishing vessel tackle mountainous seas with drunk skippers on board, these two never share a dull second. In good times and in bad, they’ll actually hardly ever get to see each other because both of them are running about like a blue-arsed fly, flitting from event to event, appointment to appointment, usually independently. Weeks can pass before they actually see each other, sometimes, which can be terribly exciting, but there is a danger that if all this chaos and travel keeps them apart for too long they may forget who the other is altogether. It’s happened before. But, then again, they will tell you a change is as good as a holiday, so maybe they’re perfect for each other?

These two are like Maverick and Goose, from Top Gun. Remember how much fun they had, and how much trouble they got it? And yes, it was a fine movie and all that, but in the end Goose got killed and we all got sad. Definitely worth the price of admission though.

Their friends are sick of them - sick of hearing that at the first hint of trouble they both just shut down and want to run away. How the hell are they going to cope with any kind of adversity? We don’t know, but hootchie gootchie, don’t they have some fun? Possibly as much fun as any duo in the Kingdom. So, advice? We have none. We just want to watch the palaver in front of us and hope we get invited to either their engagement party or their breakup party. Even then there is a chance one might become the other by the end of the night.

For better or for worse, this is high-octane duo. (8) is a bar room brawler while (7) tends to spend their time actually standing on the bar leading a group chorus. Death-defying acts are therefore not really new concepts to either of them, and we suspect the greatest hurdle these two will face is to be able to carry on their merry way without offending the other too greatly. Will they succeed? We don’t know. We suspect no one does, not even these two. In which case, if you know them, get yourself a comfy seat, make sure you’re far enough away from the fire that you don’t get burnt, get yourself a big box of popcorn and enjoy the show.

Wow, how long is a piece of string? Could these two be amazing? Yep, without a doubt. Both love the spotlight and with (7)’s fun-loving modus operandi in concert with (8)’s outspoken sense of right and wrong, although they’re not bad at hunting pure fun themselves, they can do just about anything. As a couple they are supremely magnetic and there aren’t many people who don’t know of them, even if they don’t know them personally, but behind closed doors can be a tumultuous affair, and that’s only with the two of them in the room.

One of the pitfalls of this little pairing is that (7) always wants to feel like they have the ability to spread their wings and leap from a mountain top - at a moments notice, usually - whereas (8)’s plans are more thought out, which is commendable and necessary, but they rely heavily on being able to manipulate and/coerce those around them into helping. And if the timing isn’t right for (7) and (8) insists, then it will all go to shit in a second. (7) will resent being controlled and dictated to, and (8) will resent (7) being selfish, self-absorbed and non-compliant. Both parties have a case to answer in this instance.

These two have a fine time, although (7)’s relative lack of confrontational ability means they are, once in a while, not only offended by how (8) apparently treats them, but how (8) deals with others. From both perspectives there is something to be taken away here, potentially, and maybe this is why they were/are/should be together in the first place? Make no mistakes & learn no lessons, right? This is a mantra which holds true for each of us, it’s just that, for (7) and (8) the learning of the lesson will neither be quiet nor lengthy in duration. Let’s just see how it goes…

Like it or loathe it, (7) isn’t the team player (8) is. On top of this, (7) isn’t the bull-headed leader that (8) is, and they also occasionally resent being led by anyone, even though they sometimes need it. Yes, (8) knows this and attempts to urge and assist (7) as gently as possible without making them feel like they’re under personal attack, but this gentleness will only last for so long. Anyway, that sounds pretty gloomy, but we have a powerful couple here and the stakes are raised just a little bit when compared to normal. Certainly, the noise they make is louder than usual and we have no idea what will happen. Possibly neither do they, so you’re in the dark just as much as we are. Let’s just wish them all the best, eh?

Firefighters exist because of these two. The natural prankster in (7) has a natural fixer in (9) and both tend to be glass-is-half-full kind of people. Better than that, (9) encourages (7) to at least save a little money for a rainy day, whereas (7) encourages (9) to visit the sex shop, just for the hell of it, once in a while.
However, neither are very good at dealing with stress or confrontational discussions, and at some point these moments inevitably arrive. So long as the sun is out, they avoid living anywhere near a Middle Eastern trouble spot and fresh water comes out of the tap after they turn it on, they’ll do very well.

Once again, an outstanding performance from these two. The both of them fairly float over the rink as if their skates aren’t even actually touching the ice. (7)’s melodramatic expressions as they hurl the perfectly serene (9) into the air repeatedly are, themselves, something to behold. And how (9) seems to remain so calm, that high in the air, is beyond us. Complete confidence is a must for these moves, and it’s clearly visible with these two. And did you see that last one? (9) seemed to give (7) a little wink in the slow-mo, who immediately dug their skates in before the two pirouetted out through the air, locked together as one! HOW DID THEY DO THAT! THE CROWDS GOING NUTS, AND SO ARE WE!

Did you hear how these two got together?

(7) spotted (9) across the room, who at the time was leaning against the bar in the middle of their friends, having just told some joke that had everyone chuckling. Even the bartender. 
(7) sauntered over, checked their fabulous reflection in one of the mirrors on their way there, and excused themselves as they barged into the group.
Silently, (7) pointed their finger at (9) with a grin that was cast somewhere between cheeky and knowing. 
“You. Me,” (7) said. “Let’s go.”
(9) let out a big sigh, dropped their head in mock disappointment, put their drink on the bar and said, “Okay.”
The end.

These two can entertain themselves for hours by doing seemingly very little. They find beauty and comedy in the smallest things, they encourage weird ideas in each other, the weirder the better, and they enjoy watching their partners operate and the effect they have on others. (9) is softer and subtler in their approach than (7), to just about everything, and when times are good they appreciate the differences, even endeavouring to remember to try these different approaches out. For instance, (7) will attempt to be a little more subdued sometimes, just as (9) might even attempt being a little bit grandiose. The only hitch arises here when emotional disaster strikes because both of them would prefer to run to the hills than stop and face the dilemma head on.

We always hope a couple is great in bed, but with these two it probably doesn’t even matter. If (7) is the dancing clown then (9) is the appreciative spectator and part-time assistant. Embarrassing hiccups are forgotten about quickly, painful people and situations are dismissed from their lives even faster than that and at social events they sometimes discover people accidentally milling around them. Yep, these two are potentially that good. We’ll leave it at that.

Ever seen the movie 'Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'? It’s a wonderful show about a fellow who overcomes adversity to eventually save the world from tyranny, again. Well, these two are quite similar in their desires apart from one very palpable difference.
In the movie, there is one scene were Indiana Jones is forced to make a leap of faith, which will save, not only the world, sort of, but his own father’s life. If our hell-raising, truth-or-death (8) were in a similar position they would always make the jump, whereas our gutsy-but-wired-differently (1) rarely would, which (8) would take very personally.
And eventually these ACTUAL LIFE ACTION differences will spell their doom. In short, maybe these two should just keep their clothes on.

One can easily imagine (8) as a high-ranking officer in the Napoleonic wars, ardently believing in France, and being quite happy to die for his Emperor. (1) on the other hand was conscripted and while they’re all-for France doing well, and Napoleon prevailing, not to mention how much they love their uniform and the discipline the army provides, they're mostly quite happy to simply avoid being killed or injured, to not starve or freeze to death, and to eventually arrive home in one piece with a few bragging rights. That’s enough for (1), really. Yes, (1) loves the way (8) wears their heart on their sleeve, espousing death or glory, but deep down that ain’t them, and (8) would be utterly disgusted to learn that (1) doesn’t feel the same immediate passion. In short, death or miscommunication on the battlefield is highly likely.

Mmmm, might be best if these two just kiss and call it a day. (8) is like the tempestuous rock star whose dedication to the art and to the purity of what they are singing about takes precedence, and who carries a deep mistrust of anyone on the team who doesn’t have the same belief in what they’re trying to achieve together. (1), the band manager, adores the music and the general tone of what (8) sings about, but they have a different set of passions to get involved in, and the longer they can avoid an in-depth discussion as to the philosophy of the group - something (8) loves to do, and the bigger the discussion the better - the happier everyone will be. Is it inevitable that (8) will spit the dummy?…..yep.

No, (1) isn’t a coward, far from it. It’s just that the leader of the clan, (8), is, in their opinion, certifiably insane. Currently (8) is standing on a rock preaching to the whole tribe about how, tomorrow morning, when those six hundred armed U.S soldiers come galloping over that ridge, all eighty tribe members capable of fighting are going to pick up their bows and arrows and meet them head-on. While (8) rants and raves and carries on, whipping the tribe into a suicidal frenzy, (1) drops their head and whispers quietly to no one, “You’re going to get us all killed. Why don’t we just pull back into the ravine and meet up with the next tribe?” But (1) knows that uttering such a protest right now would be deemed an act of treason. So, romance? Forget it.

The head seamstress, (1), knows what they are doing and they've been at it for a long time. Their methods are faultless, their work ethic impeccable, and they always produce outstanding results for the designers who seek them out. But have they now just about had enough? Once again (8) storms into the room waving a freshly made garment in their hands, babbling on about how this design isn’t what they specified. And it’s not the first time. (1) has tried to tell (8) that what they wanted was impossible, only because the materials in use can’t be joined together in the way they wished. But it’s no use. (8) isn’t listening to reason and is starting to get hysterical, accusing (1) of incompetence and hypocrisy. Eventually, yes, (1) tells (8) that perhaps it’s time they found another designer. They’re probably right.

These two are reasonably well-suited. (2) acts as a calming soul and the source of sound advice for the leader of the pack, (8), who in turn receives doting rock-star adulation as they crash their way through life. And this leads us to a thought: Perhaps, metaphorically, there is a chance (2) eventually feels like they are living with the belligerent and uncaring town drunk. (2) is sensitive, while, comparatively, (8) is anything but, unless you’re talking to (8). We suppose if (2) was a just a little more thick-skinned and (8) just a few notches of volume quieter, and no doubt these specimens exist in the wild, then they’d be a perfect, synchronous match. Alas, this might be hard work but both of them are used to dealing with obstacles. 
(Pssst, quick little secret: these two actually need an obstacle, so they’re better suited than they think they are, just don’t tell them that.)

So, there’s an old Chinese farmer and one day his only horse, a stallion, busts out of its enclosure and escapes. The locals hear the news and they all say to him, “Gee, that’s bad.”
“Yeah, maybe,” the old farmer says.
Next day, the stallion comes back and brings with it five wild horses. The locals hear the news and they all say to him, “Gee, you must be thrilled. You’re so lucky!”
“Yeah, maybe,” the old farmer says. 
Next day, the farmer’s son, while trying to break-in one of the new horses, falls off and breaks his leg. The locals come around and all say, “Gee, that’s bad. Who will help you in the fields now? That’s so unlucky.”
“Yeah, maybe,” the old farmer says.
Next day, the army recruiting officer comes to his house hoping to conscript his son, but leaves when he sees the cast on his leg. The locals here the news and tell the old farmer, “Gee, you must glad. You’re so lucky.”
“Yeah, maybe.” Etc, etc, etc.
Yes, it's an old story, but welcome to the non-stop roller coaster that is (8) and (2). They’ll work it out one way or another.

Many philosophers will tell you that life is one long continuous sine wave. There are ups and there are downs, and you can be certain that if life is good right now, at some point not too far away it probably won’t be, and so it goes around again. We imagine that this is what things might be like for (8) and (2) here. Disregarding their sexual compatibility, they are quite similar - passionate, sensitive and proactive - and so they have a lot in common, such that if they are in concert with each other then anything is possible. (2) is far more compassionate to the needs of others, however, and while this probably doesn’t matter for most of the time, the occasionally selfish ideals of (8) frustrate and disappoint (2) greatly. It’s as if (8) is a race horse wearing blinkers living in their own reality. Usually, with time and discussion, things are recoverable, and we wonder if it’s this too-and fro-ing actually bonds them? Although it's probably more important to (8) than to (2). We just don’t know.

If (8) is the President and ego maniac, then (2) is the speech writer who made them famous. Would (8) ever realise and acknowledge this? Maybe, but probably not. We do know that (2) is just about sick of being embarrassed by their leader, that’s for sure. After all, (2) has their own life to live, and they might be a little tired of having their lives defined by what (8) is doing. Amen.

If you imagine (8) as Rocky Balboa then (2) is their devoted and loving little trainer. If you spoke to each of them privately, they would tell you that they put up with a hell of a lot of whinging and complaining from the other person, which we suggest you all ignore. Question is, is this a fair and reasonable relationship for either of them? Well, (8) is certainly going nowhere without the attention and adulation they receive from (2) and, likewise, (2) was born to help others be better and to encourage others to greatness. So, together, will they win the heavy weight championship of the world? They’re certainly a pretty good team and it looks like we’ll all find out: Madison Square Garden, this Friday night. Be there or be square…

And suddenly we are confronted with the two drivers from a Formula 1 racing team. Yes, technically they’re on the same side, but the head driver, (8), is far more demonstrative and confrontational than (3). Don’t worry, they bring the best out in each other, but they sometimes forget that they’re trying to win the Driver’s Championship for the team, together. If they get too deep into the interpersonal rivalry then someone will begin insisting that the other driver isn’t supporting them. If this goes on for very long and isn’t dealt with then there’ll be nothing team management can do, and we might even see fisticuffs in pit lane. Either way, it’ll make for excellent television, so keep watching…

First things first - (8), pull your head in for a second. You’re not the only person who matters in this relationship. Yes, you are charismatic and usually right, but (3) is too, and they are a powerful personality in their own right. Sure, they may not love confrontation like you (8), but not many people do. So if you can just sit down for a second and shut up, we’d like to hear what (3) has to say on the issue, and we will not stand for interruptions. (By the way, we only said 10% compatibility in order to get you both thinking. Good luck!)

Okay, so we all know how (8) can act like Julius Caesar on a bad day. Luckily, (3) is no slouch and not the push-over (8) usually enjoys trying to manipulate. Yes (8), we think you’re something of a control freak, who enjoys pushing peoples’ buttons. Your issue (3) is that if you don’t lavish the right amount of attention in (8)’s direction they’ll spit the dummy anyway. Sounds complicated, huh? Anyway, you probably know this already (3) but don’t let (8) get away with too much. Half the time they’re just seeing what your limits are. You are used to excelling (3) and you’ll work them out. Buon chance!

If (3) is the successful jockey with a stellar career behind them, then (8) is the tempestuous mare who loves nothing more than trying to break a bone somewhere on their rider’s body, just to show who’s really in charge. This clashing of heads when it happens makes for splendid viewing whether they win any races or not, and to be honest, we’re not sure they will. If they can manage to listen to each other, maybe tone down their respective egos just a little, then it’s possible these two could achieve unmitigated greatness. We just don’t know, so don’t let our % estimate put you off, it’s just that, if you’re not in sync and not appreciating each others’ endeavours, you might have to get past the notion that, at some point, each of you will feel like you’re sleeping with the enemy. As ever, good luck!

And here we have another despotic leader, (8), who takes a refusal of their suggestions very badly, where as (3), the rather more humble yet equally capable Minister of Foreign Affairs, seems to spend most of their time, not concerning themselves with their own expansive and time consuming portfolio, but placating visiting dignitaries who (8) has offended, again. And we’re just about sick of this, if fact the whole population is. You figure it out (3) but if you decide to quite parliament you have our blessing. Amen.

Wow, you ready? 
When these two are good they’re incredible. They generate more sexual heat, philosophical fun and intrigue, and more overall passion than almost any duo. (8) is larger than life and inspires all those in their midst, which is terribly exciting for a wee homebody like (4). Ditto, (4) is incredibly insightful and more attuned to people’s energy, which is something (8) can really learn and benefit from.
On the flip-side, if things go to shit – i.e. (8) becomes too loud and aggressive or (4) becomes too demanding and sensitive - then you won’t find a more pathetic, bitchy, petty, quibbling couple of painful, whinging shit-heads. Who knows, maybe they actually like it that way? I guess we’ll find out…

Yep, nice. The world champion platform diver, (8), known and famed around the planet for their daredevil leaps of death-defying brilliance, and whose very core is lit-up by operating on the razor’s edge, is nurtured and propelled by their loving mentor and sage, (4), who has come to know exactly how to encourage an abet their supreme athlete. What a wonderful sight! Yes, Redbull pays for everything and no one goes home unhappy, least of all these two.

The truth: this is what these two are skilled at looking for and talking about. Yes, (8)’s approach is akin to a bull hunting for brilliance in a china shop where as (4)’s is more like trying to coax out a kitten from beneath a massive sofa bed, but at least they’re on the same page. Sexually, who knows, but relationshipically they’re a damn fine match and, certainly, (4) finds (8) a simply startling prospect who will help them break out of their shell, if indeed one exists. (8) is just happy for the encouraging audience who generally appreciates what they’re on about.

(8) is the daring acrobatic pilot and (4) is their engineer who is extremely sensitive to every sound and vibration the aircraft makes. (8) hasn’t got the attention span to deal with specifics like hydraulic pressure and oil temperature, they’re just good at flying and putting on a wonderful show. Will they crash? Not if (4) has anything to do with it. And while (8) scares the willies out of (4), there is no place either of them would rather be. Sweet!

Not often does (8) come up against someone who matches their natural desire to get to the bottom of things, and to discover what is really going on. (4) not only does that very well, but they challenge (8) regularly on an emotional level, which is unusual, and part of the reason (8) finds (4) so intriguing and wonderful. They’re actually lucky to have each other, and in all likelihood, so are we because it means we can all relax and let someone else field all thier questiions. Amen.

These two would have provided a wonderful spectacle and engendered a huge following had they been paired as a gladiatorial team inside the Roman colosseum two thousand years ago. The big, bolder and more professional warrior, (8), is perfectly complemented by their craftier, calmer and more careful ally, (5). The roar of the crowd and the sheer bloody conflict would inspire the former, while the highly technical, 3-dimensional nature of hand-to-hand battle is something the latter would get-off on. Having said that, no one has fun when they’re about to die, so perhaps these two are only meant to be together for a short time?

Can you imagine these two locked in a game of snooker? They’re both quite competitive, well, (8) is so competitive it’s ridiculous, and (5) is no slouch despite the cool exterior, but it would be a battle worth watching. True, part of (8)’s plan is to get the crowd involved and to rev them into a frenzy of support, where as (5), who has no visible opinion on this matter, is concentrating wholly on the balls on the table, calculating future events. Death or glory: this is what we have here folks, and can you just imagine the philosophical wrangling which would take place at home if they were a couple? It’d be worth paying money to watch. So, yes, on paper they’re good but in actuality we have no bloody idea. Talk to you later.

It’s not like (8) doesn’t ever help out - they’re actually an amazing, wonderful support - it’s just that they can’t do it constantly for months and weeks on end without come kind of pay back. Is this fair? We suppose it is, and we only mention it because of how dogmatic (8) is when things don’t go their way. And their capacity to have an elephant’s memory in so far as recalling what they’ve done for people, or a person, is frightening. But, all of that is rubbish when considering a partnership with (5). Why? Because (5) tells it like it is, pretty much straight away, and this is a trait (8) adores. Better than that, (5) is no fool and (8) knows this, and because they respect (5)’s opinion, despite also begrudging it sometimes, they will nearly always succumb to the truth. Got all that? Anyway, cut a long story short, these two are good. Amen.

Watching these two debate is like watching a mongoose have a go at a giant King Cobra. The mongoose, (5), is a mammal for a start, so it’s way more intelligent and it’s therefore better at making decisions and anticipating the immediate future, and it needs to be. (8), on the other hand, the big threatening presence is of course lethal, but all this posturing is only a front and (5) knows this very well. Even so, a lazy move on (5)’s behalf and it’s curtains, so they can’t let their guard down, nor do we expect them to. And deep down, you’d never know (8) is actually scared shitless right now, but we never told you that, orright? Anyway, as a couple, they’re like this all the time. They love it.

God, what a long-winded, drawn-out, melodramatic shemozzle this has turned into. The cops can’t arrest (8) just yet as there isn’t enough evidence. Detective Inspector (5) knows this, but they’re refusing to let (8) go until the hour is up, then legally they have no choice. You see, (8) really is guilty, (5) knows they’re guilty and (8) knows that (5) knows, but without any physical evidence, and without an admission, (5) is hamstrung and both of them know it. Right now (8) doesn’t mind being questioned, the cocky shit, but the whole thing is a facade. It’s like a dance, with these two, and it’ll go on until the big hand strikes twelve. 
Or until someone agrees they were once in love with so-and-so. Or until someone’s mother promises not to come next week. Or until someone admits that they were wrong. And round and round it goes. On and on and on. Thank god they’re pestering each other and not us. Goodnight.

Is that wedding bells I hear? The staunch ball-breaker, (8), has their perfect foil in (6) and it seems to be a recurring theme with these in-your-face types. What do you do?
They’re like a couple of lionesses who share the same goal of keeping the pride together. Naturally, one is more boisterous than the other because rarely in nature can two A-type leaders hold the same stage. But, it works. At least, it works most of the time. Don’t let the roars of occasional frustration fool you, nor the play-wrestles which you would swear were about to result in someone having their throat torn out, it’s just how they are and they love it.

Wow, will you look at this castle? Look at the sheer size of it! Check out those parapets! From up there you’d see the enemy coming before the enemy even knew they were going to be your enemy. Jeepers! Well, no one and no army is getting in here folks, so if you don’t have an invite and the draw bridge is up you might as well turn around and head back to where you’re from. How many people built this thing anyway? Anyone know?….Yep. Two people built it, (6) and (8). And if you haven’t seen them don’t be worried, they’re pretty careful about who they let in to their fortress of trust, mutual admiration, strength and overall brilliance although they do secretly love people coming to take photos of it. Anyway, if you do get in, somehow, can you give us a call? We’d like to interview them.

Is (8) ostensibly the captain of the ship? 
Most definitely, yes, and not even ostensibly. 
Does (6) enjoy the captain’s methods?
Yes. Indeed, as First Mate, they see to (8)’s every command with promptness and commitment to the cause. Lashings happen but they are rare. 
Does (6) ever get to take over the running of the ship?
Yes, but only when they’re in port, and as yet (8) has never been so ill at sea as to need to hand ultimate leadership over to anyone.
Does (8) trust (6)’s capacity to do a good job in such a situation?
….Yes.
Has the ship been successful in battle, so far?
They have never lost a battle, and more over, they have captured quite a healthy booty from several foreign raiders, who suddenly found themselves in the position of having bitten off way more than they could chew. (8) was apparently very impressed with (6)’s levels of initiative and courage. 
Are they due back in port any time soon?
We’re not sure. Last we heard moral was good. Crew was healthy and the captain and first mate were in fine fettle.

Yes that’s them, outside the restaurant screaming at one another in full view of the diners inside, and we suspect (8) instigated the whole thing. You see, (8) accused (6) of being a hypocrite because (6) just selected a living crayfish from the tank they’d like killed and cooked for their dinner, and according to (8), (6) raves on about the mistreatment and debasement of animals by human beings quite a bit. Anyway, what started as a gently gybe got completely out of hand, and this is what they do. Well, from time to time anyway. It’s great viewing, eh? Any second now (6) will get down on their knees and feign allegiance to their illustrious moral leader, and not long after that they’ll get in the car and drive home and shag their brains out. Categorically nothing to worry about. They’re fine.

Question: does (8) enjoy being lauded as some kind of living legend?
Mmmm….yes.
Does (6)?
Not so much.
Is (6) as capable of genius and success as (8)?
Yes.
Does (6) really believe that?
Mmmm….maybe yes maybe no, but it’s tough for them in the presence of you-know-who.
Does (6) handle confrontation as well as (8)?
No. No one does. 
Is (6) a loyal and wonderful supporter of (8)?
We think so, yes.
Can we same the same of (8)?
Believe it or not, but actually, yes. (8) is a tremendous supporter of (6) and probably their biggest fan.
The End.

For better or for worse, this is high-octane duo. (8) is a bar room brawler while (7) tends to spend their time actually standing on the bar leading a group chorus. Death-defying acts are therefore not really new concepts to either of them, and we suspect the greatest hurdle these two will face is to be able to carry on their merry way without offending the other too greatly. Will they succeed? We don’t know. We suspect no one does, not even these two. In which case, if you know them, get yourself a comfy seat, make sure you’re far enough away from the fire that you don’t get burnt, get yourself a big box of popcorn and enjoy the show.

Wow, how long is a piece of string? Could these two be amazing? Yep, without a doubt. Both love the spotlight and with (7)’s fun-loving modus operandi in concert with (8)’s outspoken sense of right and wrong, although they’re not bad at hunting pure fun themselves, they can do just about anything. As a couple they are supremely magnetic and there aren’t many people who don’t know of them, even if they don’t know them personally, but behind closed doors can be a tumultuous affair, and that’s only with the two of them in the room.

One of the pitfalls of this little pairing is that (7) always wants to feel like they have the ability to spread their wings and leap from a mountain top - at a moments notice, usually - whereas (8)’s plans are more thought out, which is commendable and necessary, but they rely heavily on being able to manipulate and/coerce those around them into helping. And if the timing isn’t right for (7) and (8) insists, then it will all go to shit in a second. (7) will resent being controlled and dictated to, and (8) will resent (7) being selfish, self-absorbed and non-compliant. Both parties have a case to answer in this instance.

These two have a fine time, although (7)’s relative lack of confrontational ability means they are, once in a while, not only offended by how (8) apparently treats them, but how (8) deals with others. From both perspectives there is something to be taken away here, potentially, and maybe this is why they were/are/should be together in the first place? Make no mistakes & learn no lessons, right? This is a mantra which holds true for each of us, it’s just that, for (7) and (8) the learning of the lesson will neither be quiet nor lengthy in duration. Let’s just see how it goes…

Like it or loathe it, (7) isn’t the team player (8) is. On top of this, (7) isn’t the bull-headed leader that (8) is, and they also occasionally resent being led by anyone, even though they sometimes need it. Yes, (8) knows this and attempts to urge and assist (7) as gently as possible without making them feel like they’re under personal attack, but this gentleness will only last for so long. Anyway, that sounds pretty gloomy, but we have a powerful couple here and the stakes are raised just a little bit when compared to normal. Certainly, the noise they make is louder than usual and we have no idea what will happen. Possibly neither do they, so you’re in the dark just as much as we are. Let’s just wish them all the best, eh?

Ever seen two elephant seals in full combat? It’s a loud, terrifying and bloody affair but rarely is anyone killed. Sure, egos might be dented briefly but, let’s face it, they each love the combat. When they’re in sync they have the potential to barnstorm any situation and achieve greatness, trusting they have a like-minded juggernaut standing next to them. Here in the real world, though, two leaders will undoubtedly, at some point, bang chests together and it won’t be in the bedroom, although that is probably a fun part of life for them, no matter how poorly they are getting on. In the end, there’s probably simply too much energy in the one room for two people to deal with.

Can you imagine Napoleon Bonaparte being married, not to Marie Antoinette, but to Napoleon Bonaparte? That’s right, neither can we, but by jingoes they’ll get a lot done while they’re together and make some kind of reputation for themselves. That part at least will a resounding success. The rest will be a disaster and many soldiers will die for no apparent reason whatsoever.

We’ve got it - a new craze which we think will be hugely popular at the speedway. What we’ll do is get two giant, super-charged semi-trailers, fill them both with fireworks, line them up at either end of the track then get them to drive at each other and collide head-on in front of the grandstand. We’ll time the fireworks to go off remotely, just before impact. What do you think? People will come for miles to watch this event, no question, and we’ll supply visors and ear muffs and small fire extinguishers. It’ll be great! Imagine the noise! Although, yes, there will be a bit of a mess to clean up, probably.

Cripes, have you ever gone and spent a few days at their house? Every single thing becomes a competition. Last night they wanted to watch different things on the tele’ and they had a full-on wrestling match in the living room. We think their kids must be used to it because they didn’t react at all. It went on for twenty minutes until the remote was accidentally tossed out the window, at which point it immediately started to rain. One of the kids fetched the remote from the front yard but the rain had killed it and there ensued a wrestle to see who was going to change stations on the TV manually, until they crashed into it and broke it. That’s when the kids started wailing, and that was it for us. We left and stayed at the caravan park.

These two are either magnificent or they are a train wreck. If they’re not on the same page and in sync with each other, they’ll whinge and spit and carry on, insisting that the other is a treacherous, lying wannabe.
