If they are, they’ll form a spectacularly powerful and capable couple who listen, advise and analyse, who communicate very clearly, and who could achieve literally anything they put their minds to. And there doesn’t seem like there is much middle ground. So, yes, good luckyou two, we hope you’re in sync and if you get to launch whatever it is you were talking about launching, we’d love an invite, as ever. Thank you, and farewell until then.

If we imagine (8) as a very powerful handgun, then (9) is the hand-crafted, velvet-lined case made especially for it. There is no doubt they are completely different people - (8) is loud and brash and in-your-face while (9) is calming and forgiving and warm - and so we expect they might compliment one another very nicely, and perhaps for a short while they will. If and when situations become problematic, however, and life does tend to toss the push bike into the bath on occasion, then this is where any complimentary notions are forgotten. (8) will want to raise hell, barge into the manager’s office no matter who is there and start tearing off wall paper with their bare teeth, while (9) will go very quiet and perhaps even turn invisible. Does this matter? Let’s find out…

Worst case scenario: The angry human, (8), storms in the door after a frustrating, miserable day at work to find the pet hound, (9), not where they usually are, bouncing around at the front door, elated to see their buddy (8), but sitting in the corner of the lounge room where they are refusing to make eye contact.  
“What have you done?” asks (8), sounding awfully grave.
“No, I haven’t done anything. Can’t we just be friends?” suggests (9)’s body language. “And please, don’t go into the kitchen.”
“Have you broken something in the kitchen (9)?” (8) asks. “Hmmmmm?”
At this, (9) scurries over to (8)’s feet and lavishes attention in the vain hope of preventing (9) from leaving the lounge room. And it’s all downhill from here folks.

These two make for a tantalising prospect. The engine room of the duo, (8), provides all the propulsion and energy for the vessel, where as (9) is a loving and attentive purser whose job is to ensure all the passengers are happy, and that they have everything they need. Storms aren’t things either they or the passengers love, while (8) on the other hand gets off on trying to smash through giant waves, the bigger the better, and they end up just getting angry if nothing seems to be happening. (9) loves the cruising life when the sun is out and when the bow is gently shooshing its way across a blue ocean so what to do? No one wants to go down at sea, and everyone is at least partly delighted to be sea worthy, but where is the delicious middle ground for these two?

Sometimes, it’s true. As much as they adore (8), and are inspired by their power and forcefulness, their never-say-die attitude and their tenacity in the face of pressure, (9) wishes, just once in a while, they would just shut the hell up and actually not insist that anyone do anything. And yes, the inverse is true, also. That is, while (8) loves (9)’s attention and appreciation, they often appear to be lacking the interest or the enthusiasm they expect and feel that they deserve. Most of all, they hate the fact that, rather than just say they don’t like something, (9) will simply change the topic altogether and totally shut down. Is it always like this? Of course not.

(8) is like a horse trainer who will do anything to win. Drugs, whippings, bribes - you name it. (9) on the other hand is just a lovely, contented horse - at least, they used to be contented - who loves running, loves the idea of a human on their back, and who wants to do well, but mostly, who just wants to eat nice grass and not necessarily get up every morning at three a.m. Especially when its freezing cold. Both of them appear to be trapped by the life they’re in, so, we’re not sure. Anyone have any suggestions?

A nice combo’. If the two of them were charged with running the company, then (1) would do the hard-nosed negotiating while (9) would ensure the employees were looked after and that the environment wasn’t being degraded too much. (9) doesn’t handle the high-powered situations like (1) and the only issue which might arise is how each of them handle the ramifications of this deep recession we’re apparently about to walk into. Having said that, they understand each other very well, including their different roles, and one would imagine that when hardship does arrive these two will ride with the punches together, laughing as they go and reminding each other of what’s important. Best of all, after coming out the back of such trials they’d be grateful they experienced it together. Splendid.

The quintessential good cop, bad cop. Good, being (9) and bad being (1), and they do their job very well. (9) is a wonderful second in charge, if you like, who has more kudos on the street in lieu of a friendlier, more engaging nature, and (1) is better at dealing with the intricacies of a case, and plotting a method to get the bad guy or fix the problem. They solve most cases they’re involved with and the Captain, back at headquarters, feels lucky to have them on board. And so do we.

(9) and (1)’s Funeral Service. Death Might Be Wonderful, is their motto. Not only do they both believe in some kind of afterlife, but they appreciate helping out here at the finish line, and to assist families through this difficult time. True, many families are a little put off by their stance but they seem to provide real care to those remaining, and the testimonies of these people are the proof in the pudding. (1) usually deals with the organisational running of the business -  schedules, embalming rosters, hearse maintenance, etc - while (9)’s role is almost purely interpersonal. They radiate warmth and compassion even when they’re alone in the bathroom, so you can only imagine how wonderful they are at consoling grieving families. Yep, Death Might Be Wonderful is doing very well, and we expect that to continue. Bless.

Don’t you just love the corner store? And how long have (9) and (1) been running it for? Feels like forever. You can see (1) at sunrise if you’re up early enough, dragging in the newspapers and stacking up the daily milk arrivals. (9) doesn’t turn up until later, ever-ready with a smile and a bit of a yarn for whoever walks in the door. (1) deals with the books, ordering stock and all the admin, and they always keeps an eye on customers when they’re out the back, just in case (9) is too busy chatting to someone to notice one of the young kiddies stealing a chocolate bar, which happens occasionally. Little does (1) know, however, that (9) is actually very aware of everything, it’s just that they think it’s rather cute and, importantly, they believe a little theiving probably teaches kids about daring and deftness of hand. Anyway, the store is going very well and the town loves them both.

The hard-nosed reporter, (1), and the travel-weary camera person, (9), have been a great team for a while now and we don’t expect that to change. (1) always has an idea about the kind of story they want to create and (9)’s advice is vital - they’ve had far more experience on the street dealing with idiotic strangers, they're better at helping people relax, let alone setting up the best lighting. On the flipside (9) never needs to suggest anything to (1) in terms of which questions to ask because they have those specifics sussed. Better than that, (1) isn’t an arrogant twat like some reporters (9) has dealth with. They’re very happy to help setting up and, overall, they just enjoy each other's company. Actually, they’re on TV right now.

Perhaps (2) and (9) were siblings, or mother and daughter or something, in a past life? It’s like a yogi master going out with a Zen Buddhist. With so much warmth, generosity and consideration in the room it’s difficult to imagine either of them raising their voice over anything. “Are they telepathic?” is a question many friends ask of them. These same friends also presume they either sleep or meditate a lot because of how utterly serene they always appear to be. In any case, maybe that’s the problem, if/when there ever is one? Surely, some time, at least one of them needs to feel the wind rushing through their metaphorical hair. And what happens then? Having said all that, these two are possibly ideal for each other.

These two should open up a clinic. They could call it, The Just Come Around And Hang Out At Our Place And You’ll Soon Feel Great No Matter What Centre. They probably wouldn’t even charge you, or maybe have a donations box out the front. In a nutshell, these two are good for each other and good for the world. Sure, (2) is the more outgoing of the duo and (9) has a more calming aspect, which both (2) and the world at large appreciates, but there isn’t much going on here which isn’t appreciated. So, we’ll let them go about their rather splendid business while we go about ours. Not much to be worried about here, kids.

What do you get when you put two rather lovely optimists together? You get a great big fluffy happy cake that everyone adores, and that very few people get sick of. Indeed, the only ones who wont like the cake are those classically cynical or antagonistic types who get off on confrontation for the hell of it. Well booo hooo to them!

One imagines Doctor (9) accidentally being seated next to Nurse (2) on the plane, for their flight to Africa, and would any of us be surprised to learn that they’re about to spend the next six months working side by side at the same refuge camp in the Democratic Republic of Congo? In all likelihood, the rest may very well be history, and you definitely don’t need to hear why these two are well suited from us. Equally, don’t ask them. They’ll just get embarrassed, especially (9).

It’s not that these two are interchangeable, but, you know, they could be. Both of them are compassionate and caring souls who tend to make the world a better place, collectively and individually, and the only real hiccup arrives when a hard decision has to be made by someone. Maybe the dog needs to be put down, or maybe there is a grandmother somewhere who is asking to be euthanised? Sounds ridiculous, but life throws up these scenarios and they have to be confronted sooner or later, so, how will these two go? (Actually, we suspect they’ll go very well, but it’ll still be interesting to see how they, or someone, deals with it. Until then though, it’s happy sailing.)

It’s as if we’re watching a sitcom. The high-powered, fretting fool, (3), trots out the door to work with humble aspirations of being incredibly industrious, generally dazzling, semi-famous and perhaps even world-changing. Later in the day they arrive home stressed and bothered, which is where our host of the century, (9), gets to tend our strident wannabe. Luckily, at home, they desire similar things in life and, yes, (9) admires (3)’s world conquering attitude, but don’t worry, this isn’t all one-way traffic. (3) admires (9)’s capacity to remain calm and their skill at producing a constant, warm interaction because they know they need the help. They might do okay, these two.

Now we’re talking. The potent bulldozer (3) in concert with the gentle and loving landscaper (9), who darts around them with daisies in their hair, removing vulnerable animals, offering water and sandwiches to the bulldozer driver, and generally making sure no one and nothing is being accidentally run over and/or killed. And (9) also takes photographs of (3)’s wonderful work so they can post them on social media later, because (3) secretly loves the adulation. Yes, it’s a little asinine for (3) to need this but so what, no one is perfect although these two aren’t far off it.

What do you get when you cross a potent leader and general go-getter, (3), with lovely warm magical glove, (9), who imparts the wearer with serene superpowers of optimism, loveliness and serenity? That’s right, you get the most wonderful and stress-free ride down the mountain side, that is so fun and tremendous you can’t really imagine doing anything else for the rest of the day. The End.

It’s not that (9) is lazy, it’s just that they operate on a slower tic, and so (3) can always help them get parts of their life in order, if indeed they require any of that. Maybe (9) needs their tax receipts organised? Maybe they even need to learn why or how keeping tax receipts is theoretically important in the first place? Anyway, as silly as some of these concepts are to (9) in the grand scheme of things, (3) is a diligent and competent cat who grasps most administrative systems very well, and who enjoys helping out when they have a few minutes free. Ditto, (9) might just help (3) relax and to appreciate the finer things in life which money can rarely buy.

Ain’t no car wrecks here folks. No smashed vases thrown against a kitchen wall. No divots above the TV where a high velocity potato has met its doom. No sugar-filled petrol tanks in anyone’s car. These two are a nice mix of power and pragmatism, as displayed by (3), and stability, humility and calm, as exemplified by (9). So only a couple of questions remain: are they getting married, and are you invited?

Respectively, (4) and (9) are on a fervent search for that soul mate who they feel ‘completes them’. Is that a corny load of unmitigated bullshit?… probably, but as it stands they might be on the right track. They’re definitely more likely to lounge around all day together rather than leap out of bed at dawn, don the matching lycra and hit the running track or the freezing beach swim. Fluffy pillows, tea and toast in bed, big long talks and gentle caresses are what’s on offer here ladies and gentlemen. 
Bored yet? They probably feed each other in restaurants, who knows. But, perhaps that lack of pure energy is what irks them in the end, if it happens.

No, we’re not in the presence of two professional pole dancers, but two professional bird-watchers who, in a perfect world, get to enjoy their ornithological pursuits while at the same time rubbing shoulders with each other. One might argue that it’s not even the birds they’re interested in, but the necessarily quiet and peaceful places they have to hide together while they list down, and occasionally photograph, their quarry. And they get to whisper to each other, which they like doing as well. Yep, it’s all good for these two.

Yes, another loving, romantic soup in the brewing here kiddies, and why not indeed!
